candidates.text:
What did we change?
[p align="start"]
[p align="start"]Utilising the mechanism above defensive tasks for end game factions have had their priority decreased, making the late game more dynamic and much more interesting to play as the Campaign AI will seek to expand and compete instead of turtling up and behaving reactively. The priority of tasks that target enemy forces is increased slightly.

How will this change affect you in-game?
[p align="start"]
[p align="start"]End game factions should be less prone to idling and clumping around a settlement, and situations where multiple end game factions end up in a stalemate (not attacking each other, only defending) should decrease.
[p align="start"]

Campaign AI Known Issues

candidates.title: Total War: WARHAMMER III review
candidates.text: I have been a fan of Total War games since Shogun 1 and have particularly enjoyed Total Warhammer 1 & 2. Unfortunately, this is just really, really disappointing.I'm not quite sure what they were thinking with the changes they made because almost all the changes are for the worse compared to WH2.The new settlement towers and barricades? Pure cancer. The towers in particular are utterly unbalanced and make every battle a slog. I say every battle rather than just "siege battles" because the AI absolutely refuse to fight you on the open field unless they outnumber you hugely. I've had three open field battles in 6 hours of play. Big, fun set-piece battles are meant to be the centrepiece of this game and this one fails at it's most fundamental level.The new mechanic where rifts into chaos randomly appear in your territories every turn? One of the most annoying mechanics they could have devised. Not only is there no way to prevent this but they take your provinces from 0 to 100 corruption in three turns, discourge enemy agents into your lands and often enemy armies. This means that the only viable tactic is to turtle and spam end turn since, if you expand, you cannot protect your provinces properly.The game economy is broken. This makes having more than one army nearly impossible (especially due to the necessary turtling) and good luck saving enough money to get decent settlements unless you farm Slaanesh's rewards.Does it have good AI? LOLNO, all AI factions at war will make a beeline for the player no matter how stupid it is to do so. This has always been an issue but it's so much worse in WH3.

How did we fix it?

candidates.title: Total War: WARHAMMER III Improving AI in Campaign
candidates.text:
Hey Folks,

At the tail end of last year, you saw us run a few of our Hotfixes out for Total War: WARHAMMER III via the Beta function on Steam. This was invaluable for our teams as we readied some necessary game updates during the rollout of Omens of Destruction, and helped us catch some last minute feedback from you and ensure our updates were on point. Whilst we haven’t needed to pull on that lever quite so much since we got back into the swing of things in 2025, it has encouraged us to think about even more ways that we can involve you in some of our more complex game changes, and work closer with you all to bring more improvements to the game.

To that end, tomorrow (February 13th) we will launch a new public Beta Branch for Total War: WARHAMMER III via Steam. This Beta will allow you to experience and provide feedback on the latest improvements to our Campaign AI, where your insights and experiences will help us refine and enhance the game. To understand what changes we’re making, you’ll read about all of the science from Principal Technical Designer Radoslav Borisov down below, and if you check back on this post tomorrow, you’ll find detailed instructions on how to access the Beta at the foot of this post.

We’ll run this Beta for around two weeks initially, bringing it to a close around February the 26th. It’ll be running on a modified version of the live game that you’re already playing today, so this Beta won’t be used to test any additional upcoming changes to the wider game, and we’ll be encouraging folks to start fresh Campaigns for this test in order to check best on how our changes are performing.

candidates.title: Patch 8.1 Now Live
candidates.text:
[img src=" everyone,

Patch 8.1 has now arrived in Total War: WARHAMMER III, with a primary focus on Campaign AI improvements, as well as introducing some new Landmarks, Technologies, and a swathe of bug fixes and adjustments across the board.

As always, should you run into any new issues after updating to 8.1, don’t hesitate to report it over in our dedicated bug reporting sub-forum.

See you on the battlefield!

— Steve Coleman // Senior Community Manager

1. Campaign AI Improvements

[p align="start"]With Patch 8.1 a number of Campaign AI changes and improvements have been added to the game:

Campaign AI Prioritisation

What did we change?
[p align="start"]
[p align="start"]There are certain Campaign AI tasks that lead to its armies clustering and idling e.g. focusing on defending key regions therefore, we’ve added a new mechanism that allows us to control exactly what the Campaign AI prioritises, depending on how many turns have passed since campaign start. Using this new mechanism we’ve de-prioritised tasks e.g. defending key regions in the late game, as contextually they are not that useful at this stage of a campaign anyway.

How will this change affect you in-game?

[p align="start"]We expect this to solve a number of cases where Campaign AI armies are clustered and idle around settlements, and the mechanism we’ve developed make this tweak also allows us to more easily solve similar Campaign AI behaviour issues in the future.
[p align="start"]

Campaign AI End Game Scenario Balance Update

[p align="start"]We’ve focused this Hotfix on bringing further improvements to many of the changes brought with Patch 6.3 and offering some refined balance changes for both Lizardmen and Tomb Kings. This Hotfix also helps to address an unintended AI behavior that was causing AI controlled factions to poorly budget their resource, and result in instances of low stack armies on your campaign maps.
[p align="start"]There’s a host of additional changes, fixes and improvements detailed below, but if you’d like to check out the changes for yourself, players on Steam can switch their client to the Beta branch and play these changes right now. candidates.title: ​Hotfix 6.3.4 - Preview
candidates.text:
Chaos Dwarf recruitment is showing a similar early sign of improvement. We’ve observed that they hadn’t been recruiting higher tier units on a consistent basis, and some of the changes that we’ve developed are giving us an early indicator that we’re starting to see some success in changing that. As with other Idle AI issues, there’s lots of testing to do here to give us a better idea of how successful we’ve been in this space, as well as a need for us to be diligent about checking that we haven’t introduced any new unintended behaviors, but from our initial limited testing, we’re progressing in a positive direction here.

Finally, Golgfag has had their Campaign AI reviewed, and has now started to show consistent interaction with campaigns. Of all of the 3 key issues listed here, this is one that we are most confident that we’re currently making a good improvement on, but still something that will require a lot more testing and plenty of careful study on Golgfags impact in a campaign.

As of today, he’s properly attacking and expanding his territory, though we’ve had a few early tests that raise concerns that he’s prone to enter a state of megabonk, and can often be found to act as quite a menace to anyone within reach. Making a change to Golgfag to get him active is a good first step, but we’re going to be doing some further balancing as part of this process to ensure he doesn’t get out of hand.

candidates.title: Hotfix 6.0.4
candidates.text:
Greetings folks!

As alluded to earlier in January, we're back with another hotfix for Total War: WARHAMMER III. Hotfix 6.0.4 introduces a plethora of fixes and tweaks to improve your gameplay experience. Here's a couple of highlights from this hotfix:

- Fixed a bug where Lords would not disengage from a settlement after selecting certain post battle options. This includes, but is not limited to, The Changeling when establishing a Trickster Cult and the Vampire Coast when establishing a Pirate Cove.
- Ogre armies can now recruit Regiments of Renown when they are within the circle of influence of an Ogre Camp.
- Fixed an issue where reinforcing AI units will be given the same order location and will clump together as they all try and pile on to complete their order.

Read on for the full list of changes...

PERFORMANCE

candidates.title: Improving AI in Campaign - Part 2
candidates.text:
Of course, there’s no guarantee that these tested changes make it into the main game, but it allows our devs to think outside the box a little and allows you to have your voices heard on what can be some pretty sweeping changes to core parts of the game.

Basically, it’s a chance for us all to work together on improving WH3 for the greater good. The Greater Good.

With this current phase of Proving Grounds, we're quietly confident that these Campaign AI changes are moving in the right direction. These new changes we're now testing for will help to show us what further refinements we need to make before we consider bringing them into the main game, and how that might impact the difficulty of our player experience.

Looking beyond this Proving Ground, we have a team internally starting to explore changes that we think we can make to Sieges, and are hoping to bring you more on that in the summer.

With that admin out of the way, it’s once again time to hand over to the almighty Radoslav. Be sure to check back tomorrow for all the details on how to access this new Campaign AI Beta!

— Steve Coleman // Senior Community Manager // Apprentice (Proving-)Groundskeeper

candidates.title: Total War: WARHAMMER III - Hotfix 4.0.5
candidates.text:
Greetings!

We're back with hotfix 4.0.5, which brings with it a round of fixes targeting critical Battle AI bugs.

- Fixed an issue with Battle AI melee target selection indecisiveness when in contact with multiple opposing units; as a result they should drop attack orders less often.
- Fixed an issue where the AI would assign a disproportionate number of units to hunt down opposing outlying units, leaving a skeleton crew to perform the main assault. We've flipped this so the AI should dedicate most of its force to the main engagement and not send its entire force to chase that one pesky outrider.
- Fixed an issue where player units with the transformation ability would occasionally trigger the AI's scouting behaviour. The underlying issue stems from how we handle transforming units, which are actually two separate units that swap places. When transforming, the AI would lose track of the original and assume it had gone into hiding, causing it to occasionally swap into scouting mode to search for Yuan Bo (The Human) while Yuan Bo (The Dragon!) was bearing down on it.
- Addressed crashes that could occur with certain units in siege battles where the AI is defending and has units that crumble, disintegrate or otherwise reach a microscopic amount of remaining strength.
- Fixed an issue with the previous Hotfix's Wood Elf outpost changes where some garrison units and effects were missing on certain buildings.

As always, your feedback helps make these changes a reality, so please keep it coming!

If you continue to experience any bugs or issues after updating to 4.0.5, please report them over on our support forums.

Thanks for your ongoing support and patience!

—The Total War Team

candidates.title: ​Hotfix 6.3.4 - Preview
candidates.text:
Before I move onto chat about other fixes and improvements that we’re also looking to make in 6.3.4, I’ll call out that right now our testing is largely focused around new campaigns, and a lot of the confidence we have today is borne from testing in this condition. We do have access to plenty of saves where these types of issues are occurring, but we currently find that the AI struggles to resolve itself away from its bad behaviors on existing campaigns where these types of problems are already present. Building out fixes that would allow for existing saves to convert into healthier states is likely something of a distant stretch goal for us, and we’re currently forecasting that to make the most of the improvements that we’re looking to make in 6.3.4, a new campaign start is likely to provide the best possible experience.

What else are we looking at for 6.3.4?

There are a host of additional changes and fixes that we’ve been tracking in recent weeks, and whilst Campaign AI and related issues are a high priority for us, there are other things that will also enter testing next week and possibly arrive as part of this update.

Here’s just a handful of those fixes, but more are in testing and whilst minor in nature, these are changes we’re keen to make alongside 6.3.4’s Campaign AI focuses.

candidates.title: Update 6 is now out on Experimental!
candidates.text:
Hi Pioneers!

Update 6 has arrived on Experimental. I’d like to preface this event with the fact that some of the new content released isn’t as far along in development as our previous Update releases, so consider this our most experimental Experimental yet! Nonetheless, we think you can have fun with everything here already and we need more of you playing with the incoming changes to help us see how far along they are and inform further development. As always, you can leave your feedback and any issues you encounter on our Questions Site: https://questions.satisfactorygame.com/

Overall, this Experimental period is going to be a little different. We will be pushing updates to finalise content that is released, and we might add some additional content along the line that did not make the initial release. With that in mind we are planning to have a longer Experimental period than usual, so don’t expect Update 6 to hit Early Access before the end of summer.

With that said, what is the content that is coming now? Update 6 shines with some major world updates, impactful changes to Equipment and the MAM progression, several great quality of life updates on the UI side of all things Satisfactory, a full overhaul of our creature AI system, and some under-the-hood changes of major systems. Let’s break that all down a bit more.

You might have already heard about this, but for the avoidance of doubt: There are no overclocking changes coming in Update 6. Also, be safe and back up your saves.

World

Spire Coast

candidates.title: Power Shard
candidates.text:
Power Shards are used for overclocking.

And also for ionized-fuel

candidates.title: UPDATE 6 info and why this update will be different
candidates.text:
The proposed change we have in mind is to make all overclocking follow a linear formula. So a machine that is overclocked to 200% would use twice as much power, and vice versa if you underclock.

Basically, what this means is that we’re thinking of buffing overclocking and nerfing underclocking a little bit. The changes to the clock speeds are intended to support players in the early game, by making it easier for them to improve their factory with overclocking without running into power increases that generally aren't communicated clearly. And for players in the late game by allowing them to build bigger and more efficient factories.

We're not entirely sure we'll make this change so please let us know what you think about this!

Release Date

With all that being said, we're still developing many aspects of the exploration update. We want to reveal the core topics of the update up front because we sort of want to set the stage for how we intend to work on the game going forward.

The obvious question on everyone's mind is of course then, "when is the update coming out?". Since we're still working on it we don't have a set release date in mind, but our current release window is sometime early June. This might change though.

I hope this aperitif of information that we’re sharing with you today is something you’re looking forward to. We’re certainly looking forward to talking more about it and showing you what we’ve done! Remember that this is a high-level explanation of the content in the update. We plan to release more info in the future to talk more about these topics so let us know if there’s any particular topic you’re excited about specifically and want us to cover in the future!

Take care until next time!
Snutter

candidates.title: Patch 0.7.0.0
candidates.text:
We’ve talked a bunch about Overclocking before and we are finally making some changes to it. If you don’t know, the Overclocking mechanic allows you to make buildings produce parts faster at an exponential power cost or produce slower while consuming exponentially less power.
The basic mechanic of Overclocking remains largely unchanged, but we’ve lowered the exponential power cost change. This means that Overclocking is less expensive than it was before, and Underclocking is not quite as cheap.
Generators are the only exception to this rule: They Over- and Underclock completely linear.

candidates.text:
These are the two new modes we added for Creature hostility which allow you to adjust how to interact with the combat aspect of Satisfactory. If you do want to fight, but want more control over the when and how, the Retaliating mode is for you. Creatures will only attack you if you attack them first, and this works per single creature. So, if you want to fight a group of Hogs or other creatures one after the other, you can do that now.

Passive mode is exactly what it says: All creatures will remain passive, no matter if you attack them or not. If you want to enjoy Satisfactory without the action aspects, Passive mode gets the job done.

You can set your preferred Creature hostility in the Escape Menu under ‘Advanced Gameplay Settings’.

In the future

This is mostly what we have in mind for allowing you to customise your experience with Creatures. In the future we are planning to implement more game modes that allow you to adjust how you play Satisfactory. But that is for after Update 7.

The basic mechanic of Overclocking remains largely unchanged, but we’ve lowered the exponential power cost change. This means that Overclocking is less expensive than it was before, and Underclocking is not quite as cheap.

candidates.title: UPDATE 6 info and why this update will be different
candidates.text:
To help tackle these new upgraded threats, improvements have been made to combat mechanics. Most notably, Update 6 will contain feature equipment changes and additions to give players more tools to engage in combat. These updates will mainly impact exploration, but there might be more equipment changes coming that will improve factory traversal as well.

Improvements to the in-game map menu

The player map will be upgraded with a range of UI improvements to make it easier to use and for pioneers to plan their expeditions and factory layouts. The Radar Tower will get an overhaul, to actually make it useful for exploration. Because it wasn’t before.

General technical improvements

There's also a couple of technical improvements to some of the underlying systems we’re currently working on that will hopefully improve the overall experience of the game for some folks. There’s also, of course, a couple of bug fixes and network improvements here and there, we’re always working on that.

(Clock Speed rebalance)

Since this update mostly focuses on the exploration aspects of the game there won't be any new production chains or anything like that, but there is one potential change we're thinking of making regarding how clock speed functions in the game.

If you didn’t know, when you overclock a machine in Satisfactory the power requirement increases in a non-linear fashion, and it’s governed by this formula
https://i.imgur.com/cwKzP9z.png

Which means that when you overclock machines, they will require significantly more power than if you were to build multiple ones and if you underclock, you will be using less power for the same part production with the drawback of slower production speed (see the Satisfactory wiki for more info on this Satisfactory Wiki).

question: What changes were made to the Action Skills for the Operative in Borderlands 3?

candidates.title: Borderlands 3 Hotfixes: October 8, 2020
candidates.text:
Today we're releasing several changes to Zane's passive skills and class mods. After buffing weapons, we started looking at how class mods were impacting the build diversity of the Vault Hunters. After investigating community feedback, we developed these changes to make more class mods viable for Zane in the end game. Most of the passive skill buffs changed today are used by class mods that had been underperforming. Additional changes to Zane are already planned, with some coming in future hotfixes and patches.

Skill Changes

Cold Bore

- Increased bonus damage[/*]

This skill only provides extra damage on the first bullet of a weapon swap. This bonus happens infrequently by nature, so we have massively buffed the damage. With this change, we are interested to see new builds centered around small magazine sizes, sniper rifles, and more.

Duct Tape Mod

- Decreased grenade cooldown by half[/*]

We found that the value of this passive skill was limited by the cooldown between each grenade, so we've cut that in half. Players will need to be conscious of the cooldown time and type of grenade mod they equipped to get maximum value out of this passive skill.

Like a Ghost

- Increased chance to ignore a bullet[/*]
- Increased the bonus for each active action skill[/*]

The stacking bonus only occurs each time one of Zane’s action skills is activated. This is infrequent in the late game, as players generally extend their action skill duration time. We’ve made this change with that play style in mind.

Trick of the Light

- Increased damage bonus[/*]

The damage from this skill depends on the number of enemies targeting Zane and Zane’s clone and can occasionally be unpredictable. To better account for this inconsistency we've buffed the damage bonus.

Best Served Cold

candidates.title: Borderlands 3
candidates.text: Improved movement system: Vault Hunters can now mantle up ledges they can't quite reach normally and crouch-slide to quickly get behind cover or get through low openings. Improved Fast Travel: players can fast travel to any Fast Travel station from the map menu without the use of one, and can also fast travel to any player-spawned vehicle on the map. Players will be spawned at the last save point if they quit from the menu and continue the game, removing the need to backtrack from the start of a map. In addition to Vault Hunters being able to revive NPCs, friendly NPCs can revive Vault Hunters. Players in Fight For Your Life can now move while being revived, and move faster when downed. Ground slams have been reintroduced since The Pre-Sequel, which can cause enemies to stagger or ragdoll. They can only be performed at a height. Knockback has been revamped, with singularity effects, ground pounds and shots from strong weapons like shotguns being capable of causing standard enemies to ragdoll momentarily. Action Skills are expanded upon, allowing characters to equip one of three action skills at any given time (except for Zane, who can equip two at once while sacrificing the use of grenades). Action Skill augments (represented by a chevron shaped icon) can be unlocked and chosen for free to increase Action Skill effectiveness, by investing skill points into the associated skill tree. Radiation has been added as an elemental damage type as a replacement/adaptation of the slag element in Borderlands 2. Enemies afflicted with radiation will take damage over time, can damage other enemies and explode upon death. It deals less damage to armor, but slightly more to shields. Cryo returns from The Pre-Sequel as an elemental effect, but" "with modified abilities.

candidates.title: Dev Update: Fine-tuning Mayhem 2.0
candidates.text:
To give your Action Skills a bigger boost, we also will add Skill Damage to Class Mods in this phase. These Class Mods will introduce powerful bonuses to Action Skills that will help with new builds and achieve the goal of letting you choose how you want to play your characters. We know the community will find the builds that do the most damage, but we anticipate a greater amount of builds made and played for fun after we make these changes. Additionally, we will look at all Anointments to enable a more even playing field between them all.

There's also the concern that chests and vending machines in Mayhem Mode do not currently spawn gear for that level of Mayhem. This will be corrected in the second phase; as it currently stands, we don’t have the ability to change it right this moment. We are in the process of creating the data for this new functionality to work and will need the time to test it along with all the other changes.

Performance and Stability

We continue to prioritize game performance and stability. Our first step was identifying Mayhem Modifiers that players reported as causing the most issues, then removing them via hotfixes until a later date. Since then, the reports of stability issues have significantly decreased. The changes that we'll make in these two phases will contain various Mayhem Mode optimizations and restore previously disabled modifiers.

Quality-of-Life Changes

Unrelated to Mayhem Mode, we’re testing some quality-of-life enhancements.

Fight for Your Life will receive the improvements we highlighted on a previous Borderlands Show. Coming in the next patch, a player’s movement will slow while they are being revived and the interactive radius around the downed player will increase to prevent them from accidentally running away from their saviors. We also will implement a particle system to indicate more clearly when a player is being revived, along with new functionality so that multiple players will be able to speed up the reviving process by all coming to a downed player’s aid.

With today's patch, we have made several changes to Zane's Skill Trees and Class Mods. candidates.title: Nominate Empires of the Undergrowth for the Steam Awards
candidates.text:
With the start of the Autumn Sale, nominations for this year’s Steam Awards are underway and we’d like to ask for your support by nominating Empires of the Undergrowth for the Labor of Love Award.

In the years since Early Access release, we’ve continued to improve Empires of the Undergrowth with huge, game-expanding updates - but we’re not done yet. We know all too well that our tiny team takes their time on the major updates, but we do that in the name of quality - and your kindness in supporting that allows us to take a considered approach. We couldn’t be more grateful, so this isn’t just our labor of love - it’s yours too!

Over the past year, we’ve been working on the following:

- A whole bunch of changes to custom games, including Skirmish - a new way to play freeplay maps.
- More up-to-date artwork for the beach and rotting log levels, bringing them in line with the visual fidelity of the more recent parts of the game - our aim is not just to finish the game, but have it be at its best possible quality too.
- Extended the climbing system to many more creatures in the game, really helping us settle into the skin-crawling feeling of ants crawling over everything!
- Working towards completing the systems and artwork for our final release, tier 5 – which will feature 3 new campaign levels set in an as-yet unrevealed location. Then a final climactic formicarium challenge which the scientist has been preparing your colony for!
- Bug fixes (ha!)
- And many more updates!

Empires of the Undergrowth Update: New Features and Changes

The latest update for Empires of the Undergrowth introduces exciting additions to gameplay, balancing changes, and a plethora of fixes and optimizations.

[previewyoutube=6tglFD103Ys;full][/previewyoutube]
Here's a breakdown of the most significant changes and additions:

Headline Features

- New Game Mode: Remix

- Play almost any level with nearly any combination of ants or termites. Custom colonies adapt to the feeding habits of the selected queen, providing a highly flexible and replayable experience.
- Accessible from the Arcade section of the main menu.

- Custom Colonies

- Create colonies with nearly any ant or termite species in the game. Custom colonies adopt traits and worker designs matching their queen.

- New Custom Game Maps

- Drive Them Back (customized for termites or regular ants depending on colony selection).

- Tier 4 and Tier 5 Achievements

- 45 new achievements for Tier 5 challenge levels, now accessible in New Game Plus.

Story and General Gameplay Changes
Level Changes

- Reduced the stun, confuse, and damage effects of sun spiders, centipedes, and emperor scorpions on Easy and Normal difficulties for fairer balance.
- In 5.2, increased casualties required for victory on lower difficulties, making it more challenging to achieve victory early.

Challenge Mode Changements

- Challenge scorpions now retain their health between days but regenerate 10% daily.
- Scorpions' escape behavior now varies based on combat location (surface or underground).

candidates.title: Fixes & Changes - First post-release patch for Empires of the Undergrowth
candidates.text:
We've released the first patch of fixes and changes for Empires of the Undergrowth, following its release into 1.0 last month. This deals with most of the more common issues that have been reported - more patches of this scale and type are likely to come in the near future.

Thanks to everyone who's been helping to test this patch in the optional beta over the past several days!

Changes

- 5.1's titans can now spawn in huge creature landmarks in freeplay
- Added a system to restore saves from backup in-game rather than manually (not yet localised)
- Added some extra protection when reloading or quitting the game when defeat rewards are being saved
- Increased save backup number to 5 (up from 3)
- Bullet ant tech tree video added
- Scroll added to behaviour toggles box (will only appear when needed)
- Added more recent localisation for Polish and Czech
- Updated lighting for custom game levels and extra levels, and changed some underground tile grids to the new ones
- Whip spider main menu icon is replaced if arachnophobia mode is active
- Added arachnophobia hats to hybrids
- Creature stat list can now show percentages to a single decimal point

candidates.title: Empires of the Undergrowth
candidates.text:
Empires of the Undergrowth was planned to be a tug-of-war game on mobile phone. The developers tried to create the game using their own homemade engine.

The first kickstarter campaign started on November 17th 2015. Although it failed, the game gained 300 backers and was greenlit to be on Steam. The developers decided to make the game for PC using Unreal Engine 4 because building their own engine proved to be too time consuming and constricting.https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/eotu/empires-of-the-undergrowth/posts/1446380

The second kickstarter campaign started on April 20th 2016, along with the release of the first demo. They reached the goal in just a week and the kickstarter ended at 180%.https://slugdisco.com/kickstarter-ends-at-180-funded/

The developers changed their approach for the game, focusing on quality over quantity. Only species that offered the most unique gameplay or combat abilities were kept in the game. Basic mmechanics were built upon the original concepts, leaning more toward simulating ant behaviors in real life. The main story was changed to take place in a lab.

The game entered early access on December 1st 2017, after a lot of delays. The reception was very positive. Freeplay mode was released on July 2nd 2018 in respond to popular demand.

Leafcutter ant update, along with the its demo mission, was released on April 25th 2019. 12 extra missions were added over the next 2 years to keep players occupied while waiting for new contents.

Fire ant update, along with the its demo mission, was released on July 27th 2022. The game went through major aesthetic changes in 2023 after new artists joined the team.

Hooded Horse became the new co-publisher for the game in 2023.

candidates.title: June 13, 2023 Patch
candidates.text:
Lifeweaver unlock challenges added.
Lifeweaver can now be unlocked by completing all his challenges!
Incomplete weekly challenges will no longer reset to zero. 100% of the progress made in weekly challenges in the previous week will be kept and carried over.
All weekly challenges requiring wins have been converted to "Complete games. Wins grant double progress."
This change results in the required amounts becoming higher, but the average total number of games needed to complete the challenges has not.

Developer Comment: Our goal is to ensure every game played contributes to weekly challenge progress. With the progress carry-over change, when weekly challenges reset, all progress on incomplete challenges will be carried over into the next week. Completed challenges will still reset.

The change from winning games to completing games increases the required amount to complete, but the average number of games required for completion remains the same. For example, "Win 10 games" could take any number of games to complete—around 20 games on average—and "Complete 30 games. Wins grant double progress." takes between 15-30 games, also averaging around 20. While this increased number of games looks big and scary, the maximum number of games it takes is now capped, and the average remains the same.

candidates.title: WORLD OF HORROR review
candidates.text: A big "don't recommend" simply for how unenjoyable and bulls**t the "challenges" are. I would normally just ignore those things altogether, but of course the dev had to go and make them mandatory to unlock the secret playable character. It's not just that they're hard - with the Old Gods being random and difficulty always set on "hard mode", things that could change to make them more bearable -, but because they're a painful slog to get through, as well. The entire idea behind each of the challenges is "What if you had to play on hard mode with a character that's deliberately deprived of what makes playing them tolerable?" Not to say they're all equally hard, or equally boring to play through, but enough are, and there's a lot of them. I don't wanna spend hours upon hours trying and failing to get through those things just to unlock the character, therefore I do not recommend this game.

candidates.title: Challenges
candidates.text: Lifetime challenges are permanent, and do not reset. They are often far more time consuming and require more effort to be put into them to complete them, for the most part. Lifetime challenges are split into two categories: General and Story Missions. General challenges are further split into New Player challenges, which reward players for their first wins in various game modes with Battle Pass XP, Player Title challenges, which require players to win a certain amount of games in each mode to receive a unique Player Title and Hero Mastery challenges, which are related to the Hero Mastery game mode and mainly award Battle Pass XP. Mission challenges are related to the purchasable Story Missions and reward various cosmetics alongside Battle Pass XP.

candidates.title: TranZit
candidates.text:
Persistent Upgrades
New persistent upgrades, colloquially called "Perma-Perks" by fans, are a new feature in TranZit. Persistent Upgrades are perk like effects earned through specific actions and lost through similar actions. Assuming they aren't lost, players will keep them even through a full death and will start with them in a new game of TranZit or even Die Rise and Buried.

These upgrades stack with any Perk-a-Colas, meaning the player can get even faster revives by obtaining the appropriate upgrade and buying Quick Revive for example.

When the player obtains an upgrade, a green flash will appear on the screen, and the character will comment about it. When a player loses an upgrade, the game will play an eerie noise.

candidates.title: Challenges
candidates.text:
Challenges are designed to provide achievements for the player to aim towards, and unlock heroes as part of the First Time User Experience. Completing challenges rewards the player with Battle Pass XP and/or cosmetics.

Challenges reset on different timings, featuring daily, weekly and seasonal challenges. Additionally, there are various lifetime challenges that can only be acquired once. At the end of each match, challenges the player has made progress on during the match will be shown with a visual representation of the remaining progress.

Most challenges cannot be completed in Custom Games or Practice vs AI. Players can filter challenges by completed, uncompleted or in progress. Total Mayhem and co-op modes are also exempt from most challenges as the ability to deal damage or heal is significantly easier in that mode due to the higher HP pools and reduced cooldowns. Junkenstein's Revenge and other co-op modes will grant Arcade wins.

Select challenges are displayed in the Main Menu, primarily related to an ongoing event. Further details of the challenges and their rewards can be inspected in the Challenges Menu.

candidates.title: Prestige Mode
candidates.text:
In Call of Duty: Advanced Warfare, there were originally 15 Prestiges with 50 levels each. Once a player complete level 50, they can enter Prestige which reward them with a permanent unlock token, a new emblem and calling card as well as an additional Create-a-Class slot for the first five Prestiges. They are also rewarded with one gear of the "Sentinel Recon" outfit for every Prestige up until Prestige 8 and one gear of the "Atlas Tier 1" for every even Prestige with the last piece unlocked at Master Prestige. The weapons will once again be locked by their level and their camouflages challenges will be reset for the camos that were not earned before prestiging. The total amount of experience required to enter Prestige Mode is 1,002,100.

On March 3, 2015, 15 new Prestiges, dubbed "Master Prestiges" were added into the game. Like regular Prestiges, the player is rewarded with a permanent unlock token, a new emblem and calling card every time they enter a Prestige. However, the challenges and weapon camouflages aren't reset after each Prestige. The player will also unlock an Elite variant for a weapon with each new Master Prestige reached. Once a player reached the final Master Prestige, called Grand Master Prestige, they will unlock the "Grand Masters Prestige" outfit.

candidates.title: Halloween Update
candidates.text:
Try to unlock them all in Classic Mode and build fantastic vivid worlds in the Creative Mode.

New Challenges

Of course, new Special Tiles also bring new challenges! A total of 6 new challenges, one for every new Special Tile, are added to the game. On top we added a few more levels to already existing Challenges, which give you a total amount of 34 Achievements to unlock!

- Planner - Score [x] perfect placements at once.
- Explorer - Connect [x] preplaced tiles in total.
- Flag Collector - Complete [x] flag quests in total.
- Heavy Weight - Place [x] consecutive tiles without rotating a tile.
- Quest Master - Complete [x] quests in total.
- Analyst - Collect [x] points with a single tile placement.

Other Additions

That is not all, though! We have also added many other small features to improve the gameplay experience in Dorfromantik.

You can now adjust your various camera speeds - Scrolling, Zooming, Rotating - in the Keybinds Menu with ranges from 0.2x to 5x standard speed. We hope this makes traversing larger maps easier, or allows you to record those slow, cinematic shots of your creations!

We now have in-game statistics! these are on a save-by-save basis and include statistics like Playtime and Placed Tiles. These also work for older saves, so now you can finally find out how long you worked on those giant landscapes worth hundreds of thousands of points, and just how many Tiles you placed.

Outlook for the rest of 2021

So, November and December will be a bit lighter on game updates. We have mentioned it a couple of times in the past, but the core team is diving into their Master Theses starting next week. They will still be working some hours on Dorfromantik every week, but obviously their priority will be fixing bugs and outside of that, smaller stuff.

candidates.title: Important: About MODs and 1.0!
candidates.text:
[img src=" and Pocketpair support modding, and we're grateful to all our fans who have dedicated time into modding the game up now. We look forward to seeing all the amazing MODs that will be made after 1.0.

However, if you haven't played the game in a long time then it is possible you may have old and potentially harmful MOD data still on your PC.

The upcoming 1.0 update for Palworld makes significant changes to the game’s systems. If you still have MODs installed from the past, especially MODs that have been left installed since around 2024, you may encounter problems such as:

・Crashes when launching or playing the game

・Corrupted save data or save data failing to load

・Quests or events becoming impossible to progress

Please Note! Simply turning MODs “off” or “disabling” them is not enough.

MOD files and MOD loaders that remain in the game folder may still be loaded when the game starts, even if they have been disabled, and can cause issues. Please manually delete these files before updating. If you have ever installed MODs in the past, even if they are currently turned off, please make sure to delete the files.

Recommended steps before updating

(1) Back up your save data

(2) Manually delete old MOD files from the game folder. \[Most Important!]

If any of the following files or folders remain, please delete them or move them to another location. Simply disabling them with a MOD management tool will not delete them.

Please check these guidelines for instructions on how to remove mods: https://guideline.palworldgame.com/palworld-mod-guideline

(3) Verify the integrity of your game files on Steam

Steam Library → Right-click “Palworld” → “Properties” → “Installed Files” → “Verify integrity of game files”

(4) Confirm that the game launches correctly in an unmodded state before applying the update

candidates.title: PATCH 01.000.400
candidates.text:
Freedoms Greetings Helldivers, I'm your host Release Captain Carlberg bringing you democracy's latest and greatest from Super Earths superior minds. Its a lot of information so lets dive in!

Overview

For this patch, some of the major areas of interest are

- Visible Supply Lines & Attack Origins in the Galactic War.
- Stratagem, weapon, planet, and enemy balancing updates.
- Various crash fixes, stability improvements, and other updates.
- Invite-only lobby creation.
The right most option in the Lobby settings. Currently only localized in English. Additional languages coming in the next patch

Balancing

Goal with stratagem balance changes this patch:
With these balance changes we wanted to buff up some of the weaker stratagems to make them more viable and add more possibility for variety in the loadouts. We also changed a few to make them more consistent, but the goal was to keep a similar or higher power level.
We are looking into the stratagems more to see if there are any other stratagems that might need some buffs or changes to make them more viable. We also want to be better at explaining what our goals are with the changes, please see the linked blog post for more information.

A/MLS-4X Rocket Sentry

- Decreased spread
- Prioritize larger targets
- Increased target distance from 75 to 100m
- Decreased Rockets per salvo 2 to 1 (to get a better ammo economy)
- Increased explosion radius from 1m to 4m
- Decreased explosion armor penetration (Explosion can no longer damage heavy armored enemies. The projectile still has enough AP to damage heavily armored targets.)
- Increased projectile damage from 200 to 300

A/MG-43 Machine gun sentry

- Reduced cooldown from 180 sec to 120 sec.

candidates.title: PATCH 1.000.400 explained
candidates.text:
Helldivers!

Johan Pilestedt here, now in the Chief Creative Officer position at Arrowhead. First, I want to thank you, the community, for clearly voicing your opinions and concerns for the balance and fun of the game. With that, we have gone over a lot of the Weapon and Stratagem balance in our latest patch (01.000.400), and we wanted to share with you a little more information on the decisions we made.

With these balance changes we wanted to buff up some of the weaker stratagems to make them more viable and add more opportunity for variety in loadouts. We also changed a few to make them more consistent, but the goal was to keep a similar or higher power level.
We are looking into the stratagems more to see if there are any other stratagems that might need some buffs or changes to make them more viable. We also want to explain why we are making the changes we do, so that you can follow our thinking.

A/MLS-4X Rocket Sentry:
The old intent was to saturate an area with rockets, but it made it too inconsistent against medium and larger enemies.

We want to make it more consistent against medium and larger enemies and give it a better ammo economy to separate it from the autocannon sentry that has a higher damage output, but can waste ammo by shooting targets that are already dead.

A/MG-43 Machine gun sentry:
The Machine Gun Sentry felt like a worse version of the Gatling sentry and we wanted it to have a different place in the tool box.

We lowered the cooldown to make it more available and more useful when changing position often.

candidates.text:
[previewyoutube=Dupl3lr2UBk;full][/previewyoutube]Freedoms greetings citizens of Super Earth! Im your host Release Captain Carlberg bringing you the latest and greatest from high command. So without further ado let us dive in.

Overview

The final part of our 60 day commitment is here!
This patch marks the last set of changes we aimed to implement for the 60 day community commitment while also addressing issues we previously didn’t have time to fix.

So what does this patch contain?
We have made changes to the remaining weapons and stratagems we weren't able to finish for the patch on September 17th, ensuring they’re now more interesting and effective. We have also dedicated some time and we’ve looked over some key core systems like enemy spawning as well as targeting and vision for the Automatons. Based on your feedback, we’ve fine-tuned the Automaton experience to hopefully make them feel less frustrating to play against. Additionally, we have also adjusted the Helldivers durability to make your armor choices feel more impactful.

Finally, we've introduced new functionality to certain items to give players more depth in mastering their equipment. For example, the GR-8 Recoilless Rifle and the AC-8 Autocannon now have programmable ammunition, and drones that come with backpacks can be toggled on or off for added control.

We hope you enjoy these changes! The team at Arrowhead has been thrilled to work on this 60-day commitment for you, our community and players and seeing your reactions to the work we’ve done! Together, we aim to ensure Helldivers 2 delivers on its core fantasy and remains a game we all love to play.

candidates.title: v1.4.7 - The Parsing Optimization and Bug Fixes Minor Update!
candidates.text:
Dear Stormworkers,

This week we release a minor update entirely focused on bug fixes and quality improvements!

This update is the latest in a campaign of quality focused minor updates, and we have more planned for the future.

The main quality improvement is a change to how we save vehicle files - this change is backwards compatible so your existing vehicle files still work the same - but vehicles will now saved with a better compressed format, meaning their size on disk is now smaller. This has several benefits to players - some players with lower spec PCs are less likely to run out of memory if they don't have much RAM, saves are generally smaller, and vehicles should spawn faster in multiplayer.

In the patch notes below, you will see a lengthy list of all the changes we have made for this update. Some of the patch notes include an #issue number which relates to the issue id from the issue tracker. We are trying to provide this extra info so players can better see what has prompted the change, as well as look at the official issue tracker to better understand the discussion around the change.

This also clearly shows what is driving bug fixes and improvements to the game - the clear and concise issue reports that players submit - so thank you to every player who submitted an issue relating to the below. We are really pleased to have made these improvements to the game, and so thank you for your help.

This week we have been made aware of some networking issues caused by the new physics based fish system. While we were unable to patch this issue for today's update we are working on a fix that we hope to deliver by next week. In the meantime we recommend that server hosts disable wildlife in general settings to prevent network slowdown. Thank you for your patience and helping us out by reporting bugs to the issue-tracker site.

candidates.title: Update EB 0.57 - The Control Update
candidates.text:
Support for over 500 games. Automatic sensitivity conversions. Support for direct CM/360 input and Focal Distance scaling. And a whole host of other changes.

Welcome to the Control Update.

The Control Update

The control update is a fundamental rewrite of the way the "Control" section of Aim Lab works.

This update brings a myriad of new features such as fully automatic sensitivity conversions, scaling by focal distance (See our most recent blog post for more information on this) and the ability to input your raw CM/360 instead of playing around with sensitivity.

This means that you can now change from one game to another without having to reset all of your sensitivities - Instead, they will now match automatically.

We have put together a short blog post to help newer users to understand how to use the Control Update more effectively - So if you need a little help to wrap your head around some of the myriad of new features the Control Update brings, check out the Control Update Guide!

New Feature

Key Fixes

- Added support for Unreal PSO Caching (shader pre-compiling) to address and reduce the amount of shader stuttering experienced on PC.
- Made several improvements to framerate in key areas of gameplay on all platforms.
- Made a number of graphical fixes and improvements across the game on all platforms.
- Resolved multiple issues that would cause the game to crash or soft lock during gameplay on all platforms.
- EA SPORTS™ WRC can now be launched on Steam Deck.

Accessibility

candidates.title: Dakar Desert Rally review
candidates.text: Dakar Desert Rally feels like a proper game release now.While it still doesn't run great, the huge stutters seem to be gone and driving the vehicles on a gamepad has greatly improved.I hope Saber keeps improving the game's optimization and, personally, I also hope they allow for even faster steering response in the next updates since it's still a bit on the slow side.On the topic of controls, the countersteering has improved on all vehicles, but it can still be a bit unreliable at points, likely due to it still being a touch slow.Otherwise the driving feels absolutely stellar. The grip makes sense, even if a bit high, the vehicles react well to jumps, you can feel the weight shift, and in general the bikes feel like bikes and the cars and trucks feel like cars and trucks.All in all, it's an amazing offroading experience with a huge playground to mess around in.The issues with wheel support have been fixed too, I can plug in my wheel and configure it without any trouble now.Some weird design choices are still there. When playing on the Sport mode that allows you to play the game like Sega Rally, when a vehicle gets ahead of you it's impossible to see due to the dust.If the point of the Sport mode is to make the game more accessible to a more casual audience, you should be able to see better when behind another vehicle in this mode, like in other arcade rally games.You can now start a quick race without going through the online lobby system, like any other game.Pick a vehicle, pick a location, and just have fun.They've also added the ability to pause the game midrace (because it's not online anymore) and it's possible to skip a part of the race start sequence.Sadly it's still an AI that launches your vehicle, you cannot rev it up yourself and launch it the way you want.

question: Why might someone not recommend the game 'Unpacking' despite enjoying it?

candidates.title: Unpacking review
candidates.text: This is NOT a negative review, I am merely saying I wouldn't recommend this game due to the price/hour played balance. I played for 2.7 hours, which Steam lowers to 2 hours. I'm gonna say I played for 3 hours. If I were to have 1 hour = 1 euro, I'd have to play another 17 hours to at least be even money-wise. I didn't speedrun this either, I just am a quick organizer.A great fun game that's surprisingly relaxing and manages to put in a story through the environment and the items the player unpacks. It's really cute with the artstyle, and the different types of accommodations the player goes through as we go through the character's life is a fun gimmick to keep things fresh. Seeing recurring items especially feels quite realistic, we all have our items we take with us through our life. The problem is that this game's only reason for replaying would be to acquire all the achievements. Personally I don't feel like unpacking everything again or putting things differently to enjoy the game again - I've experienced the (brilliantly executed) story already and enjoyed seeing the items and what they may mean for our character. I loved this game, but the price definitely felt a bit too steep for how short it truly is. Great concept though, nothing put praise for it!

question: How does the initial resource distribution affect the early game in the game Terraformers?

candidates.title: Terraformers review
candidates.text: The map you're on. The cards you draw. The resources that surround you. This mechanic called "expectations" which, if it gets out of control, will be ultimately what ends your game. So you have to frantically build ahead of these expectations and hope you get the right cards, have the right resources nearby to make this all happen.The roguelike element helps to unlock more cards but that's in and of itself a bit of an issue because it keeps you from getting the cards that you really need. In my first game, I couldn't draw a card to increase power to save my life. No power = no exploration. No exploration = no expansion. No expansion = can't stay ahead of expectations. The second game was similar but with orbital options, which cuts out a lot of specialty things. The game is hard. I didn't come close to winning even the very first scenario. And while I'd like to try an easier, more relaxed version of this there seems to be no difficulty settings. Card game + roguelike + difficult with no settings = not for me. If you want a roguelike card game based in space I'm sure you could do a lot worse. If you're looking for a strategy city builder then this isn't the game you're looking for.

candidates.title: Terraformers review
candidates.text: 我觉得还不错，算是近期把rougelike元素和回合制种田结合得比较好的游戏。事件分布也比较有节奏感，每一个“下一回合”都充满着期待。但瑕疵还是有的，一些bug部分不谈。只谈设计方面的问题。由于游戏在区域和卡牌上有着双重随机要素，使得开局非常吃运气成分。例如在初始区域就有水、硝酸盐等前期发展所需资源，则前期扩张速度会远远高于没有这些资源的开局。而卡牌抽取则影响了建筑规划，前期卡牌不合理可能直接卡死扩张速度。而后期则有可能产生部分资源过剩却无法发展的困境。我是遇到过粮食堆积超过200，但愣是完全抽不到人口建筑和机器人建筑，导致根本无法扩张的情况。这使得其他资源也堆积着无法建造。个人建议是在游戏中加入每回合可以重新抽取一次卡牌机会的科技建筑或者可以定向产出所需卡牌的科技建筑来降低由运气带来的运营困境。如果游戏中已经有而我还没解锁的话，可略过这一条。另外也建议增加一些可以将积压资源快速转换成其他资源的方式，即使是亏损一定资源，以此规避某些资源产出过剩，而另一些极其紧缺的问题。虽然这个问题可以通过规划来规避，但由于地块和卡牌所需资源的随机性以及后期资源增长速度远高于贸易。使得某些资源大量囤积而花不出去。例如出现3位数硝酸盐与1位数硅酸盐的情况。如果游戏能把运气成分和规划成分再调整一下的话，会非常有趣味。否则一味通过不停调高满意度来逼迫玩家这并不合理。

candidates.title: Terraformers review
candidates.text: 无论是前期、中期还是后期，各阶段玩家的各项资源都是稀缺的。 资源类型很多，包括粮食、电力、科学、水、硝酸盐、硅酸盐、钛金属和氚，而玩家发展城市所建造的各类建筑、城市外建设各类设备设施、新建城市等等，对所有的资源的需求量都极为庞大。 资源的获取只有探索获取、建筑生产和星球贸易。 但是，探索需要消耗电力、建造建筑需要大量各类资源、星球贸易的线路增加亦需在城市外建设更多的的设备同样会消耗诸多资源。 有得必有失，因此，玩家必须考虑将每一份资源精打细算，用到正确的地方，逐渐形成资源增长且不影响民众支持度的良性循环。 游戏采用回合制策略形式、点线网状型探索地图模式，让玩家步步为营，逐步实现火星改造的大计划。 每一个回合，玩家能够通过消耗电力，从任一已探索的区域点向下一个点进行线性延伸探索，探索点距离城市越远，消耗电力越多。 不同的探索点，其地形、资源产出也各不相同，这些由电脑在每局初始随机生成。 在平原、熔岩山、环形管这类地形中，还可以建设新的城市，形成新的中心，进一步辐射到火星的四面八方。 玩家将带有问号的未探索点解锁后，可以通过从任一城市向外辐射，逐步占领相邻区域领。 不同城市间的延伸占领线路不能互通且会阻拦，因此，玩家在占领点数有限的情况下，需要合理规划每一座城市延伸出的占领线路避免点数浪费，（占领所需点数则需通过提升城市的人口数量获取）。

candidates.title: April devlog: Changes between the Prologue and Early Access
candidates.text:
As mentioned in the previous devlog, the game now has a goal which is different depending on each scenario. There is no limit to the number of turns you can play but you must reach the goal before your total support reaches 0. Winning a game often takes about 60 to 70 turns. With all the new elements to consider this will usually take a few hours. Some examples of goals are: “fully terraforming the planet” or “getting a specific amount of prestige from spreading life” or “mining a specific amount of resources”... And in addition there are multiple difficulty levels per scenario. This makes replaying the game more varied and provide more interesting challenges.

The new goal bar above your current population support.

We’re very excited that the game will finally release so soon, and would like to thank everybody again for playing the Prologue and supporting us!

See you in a week with the game’s EA release!
Terraf Team

candidates.title: Terraformers review
candidates.text: Great game. Great repleyability. And it is in Early access. It is frankly almoust scarry how good it can be when finished...

candidates.title: Terraformers review
candidates.text: Well, the usual resource-management. You'll also get resources by exploring the planet.There are different locations for those projects. You have some for cities, others need to be outside the cities and then there's projects in space. You expand your cities by building homes for your people (or robots) and have to take care to get/keep their support.Then there are also leaders you can choose, which give you certain benefits. There's a lot of choices to make in this game. Plus there are also events sometimes, from sandstorms damaging your buildings to golden science years speeding up your research.There's no endless mode currently, you play scenarios which end as soon as you've reached your goal. There are different paths, that have a different focus, and each has multiple difficulties which you unlock by winning easier games.The only thing I'm missing right now is an endless mode, because I didn't really get to do a lot of terrforming yet (I just started my 3rd game). But it's pretty early on the roadmap, so that's gonna be there very soon.I love the art style and how many different kinds of projects there are already and that you unlock even more as you progress. I'm really looking forward to the planned additions, but already have that "just one more turn/game" feeling as it is now.There is a roadmap already, so if you see anything on there you really want, I suggest waiting for a bit. There's also a demo (Prologue) that you can try if you're not sure.Also, the devs are very responsive on Discord, which is usually a good sign.

candidates.title: Tariq Fayed
candidates.text: Tariq's Overwork ability, while sometimes helpfull, has two major drawbacks: 1. it can only be used once per city and 2. with Tariq being an early game leader, the resource gain from the ability is likely to be limited. On the other hand, his Police Station building is great, since it allows to offset early penaltys for Living quality (like low temperatures) and will scale in the later stages of the game if the population of the city is increased. His Specialization, like most early Game Boost specializations has the ability to provide a significant boost in Water production in the end game, especially with water being one of the more readylie available resources later on with some provinicial and oceanic buildings providing large amounts of water.

candidates.title: Terraformers review
candidates.text: Arguably more board game than video game, Terraformers is a turn-based, resource and hand management game in which you establish colonies on Mars with the aim of reaching your chosen scenario goal. The first 25-ish turns are about building up your resource production in the most efficient way possible. You don’t necessarily need everything straight away, but there’re definite priorities you’ll get the gist of after a few games, which unfortunately makes the early game a little repetitive. Once you’ve got some production going then the game lets you get a bit more creative as you decide how you want to pursue the scenario goal.There’re seven scenario types, with increasing difficulty levels for each, though they’re all the same. For instance, the Blue and Green Paths are both terraforming focused, while the Red Path and Expansionist scenarios are expansion themed. As you increase the difficulty then the nuances between each one become more apparent as you’re pressed to play more efficiently, but the different goals are really just shifting your priorities within a given run. For example, in the expansion scenarios you can slack on terraforming and space efforts somewhat, but you’ll still end up doing a small amount eventually because the benefits you get from them are typically still important enough (or even necessary) to warrant some investment. Overall, this can lend runs a same-y feel to them, particularly with how predictably the early game plays out each time.If you can stomach the repetitiveness then there’re a lot of meaty decisions to make, particularly when playing at an appropriate difficulty for your skill. Furthermore, the pacing feels good.

candidates.title: Terraformers review
candidates.text: Terraformers is an... game. I enjoyed it, I think it does a lot of things very well, but it has some rough edges and balance issues.As someone who enjoys 4X games like Civ but doesn't like the combat element, Terraformers is a great experience. There's events you have to grapple with, but none of them involve other empires trying to steal your land and kill your people. In fact, pretty much any hold you solidify remains yours for the entire game. Thus, part of the challenge is strategizing how to proceed in a way that won't undermine your later efforts.One thing Terraformers does that I really appreciated is it injects an almost roguelite element - you have different scenarios with different goals which you can keep ramping up, challenging your own times, and win experience for. The experience unlocks new buildings, projects, and leaders as you go (current cap is level 34). As someone who theoretically to replay Civ as a conqueror or religious leader but keeps getting boxed in, this is a really nice feature. If you want to go greedy resource-grabber mode, there's a challenge for that; one for terraforming, ecology, science, expansion, space projects, etc.The game does have some awkward elements. The constant raising standards for Support applies a natural pressure, but sometimes it can get out of hand with little recourse. Some random events are so resource-intensive that they can change the scope of the game in one turn (ie the Earth crisis, which I pretty much always either take the embargo hit on or just restart). It is pretty easy to get comfortable and never use certain cards. Some effects don't synergize in ways that totally make sense - especially terraforming, I'm confused on why we can only have 1 animal in any zone.

candidates.title: Terraformers review
candidates.text: 游戏存档只能保存当前进度，每次存档都会把之前的存档覆盖。 初入游戏的游玩体验让我觉得有点类似冰汽时代，开局都是在一个坑里，然后生产食物增加人口，在城市周边地点进行探索获取资源，资源用于建设城市内的建筑设施。 特别是开局选领袖时有个人有加班技能（降低民众支持度以换取额外的生产资源），一下就让我把这俩游戏想到了一起。 但玩着玩着发现仅仅是视觉上类似而已，实际玩法差的挺多的。 游戏中不需要考虑时间问题，领袖的探索技能只依靠电力，越远电力需求越大。 探索的资源是马上入库的，即使是人造卫星固定3回合CD，探索的资源也是马上入库的。 游戏中建造设施也是资源够了马上建成，直接投入使用。 这点我玩着觉得蛮不错的。 游戏通关的方法应该还蛮多的，因为决胜点影响因素就很多，只要偏向几个因素大力发展，应该都能过。 我通的这局偏向提高居民支持度，然后资源平衡生产，稍微改造下环境就通了。 游戏不算复杂，像我这种没啥基础的玩一会也能上手。 虽然环境改造的一些东西没搞懂，不过应该只是提供不同方向的通关方法，不影响游玩。 游戏有好几个难度，居民的期望和决胜点要求可以调整的。 我通的倒是最简单的难度。 游戏非常适合打发时间，或者是摸鱼啊，琐碎时间游玩。 有事的时候直接放着不管就好了，暂停都不用。 我的游玩时间20小时左右，抛去挂机的时间，也玩了蛮久的。 1. 游戏的随机事件类型太少了，我玩了3局，基本上见到的随机事件都是火星地震、沙尘暴、探索到别人剩下的补给箱。 好歹是扩殖一个星球欸，随机类型不得多弄一些吗。 科幻性质的来一些2.

candidates.title: Pekai Ayad
candidates.text: While Pekais abilityss allow for an early boost in support income, the impact of them is limited in the long run. The bonus of +3 Support for a building space without adjacency boni is easiely overshadowed by mid to late-stage buildings and the bonus gain of 2 support per turn per new city does not scale well with the later rise in demand, making the Specialization nearly useless in later stages of the game. Her Industrial Lobbying ability gives a small boost of every minable resource, but the resource gain by exploration of a new tile, will in most cases be higher in the net gain of resources and be more targeted towards the resources needed in the current situation, if the neccessary resource is available to explore.

candidates.title: Terraformers review
candidates.text: 这是一款拥有多种玩法内容且带有特色的回合策略游戏，主要是进行火星殖民，之后充分利用火星资源改造火星，把火星改造成另一个美丽的绿色星球，正所谓要想生活过得去，火星就得带点绿~ 领袖是每十年（十回合）换一任且不得连任，每个领袖自带一个探索星球的标准技能和其他两个主动和一个被动专属技能，因此，在有限的回合内发挥该领袖的最大效果才是最重要的。 前期建议先不要选改造基因和提供太空项目的，根本没有能力去用，到第三任领导人再考虑。 选择随机建筑抽卡这一块，优先选择农场或者电场，然后有加成建筑选加成建筑，因为比较难抽。 我有一局，第三个回合没选土壤工厂，然后就再也没见到过了，关于人口建筑的话，个人喜欢优先建设第二座城，然后再扩建人口建筑。 还有建城有条件少选平原，辐射大支持度得的少，沙尘暴坏的东西比较多。 建筑这一方面优先造建筑群，也就是三个或四个资源产出建筑，中间放一个资源加成建筑，如果开局的图只能造一个建筑群的可以重开一把。 一般倾向于优先造电和粮食，科技建筑在第一个城市里一般不造，因为一开始的目的主要是探索和扩张，我到后期他其他资源一般都只有几十的情况下，科技能剩个好几百。 城外一般优先扩张有资源的地方造矿场，然后如果你有望远镜和太阳能电厂也可以选山峰，另外，观光塔少造点，个人感觉稍有一丢丢亏。 区域改造主要是看右边那四个参数，要么完成太空竞赛项目，要么通过放置部分细菌和特定的建筑来进行提升，只有海洋最为特殊。

candidates.title: Terraformers review
candidates.text: Early Access Review - Initial release weekendI encountered NO bugs in over 5 hours of play on a Launch product. STRANGELY SATISFYING.I am reviewing the product as-is, and I imagine it will only get betterThis game is already an excellent play, especially for the price. I play a LOT of strategy games, I own a wall full of board games. This definitely has the feel of a board game, from the technology cards you draw each turn, to the action-based turn play. But it has too much going on to truly track in a board game format. You build up multiple cities, constructing housing, food production, entertainment, and their outlying territories, from exploring for resources, exploiting those resources with mines/observatories/power plants, and managing city comfort. There are also space projects to export resources for (and spaceports for doing so, or for trading with earth). You also have leaders with specialties (like extra water for every 3 water you produce, or extra research benefits for keeping happiness over a certain number), and those specialties last for the whole playthrough. The leaders also have unique actions you can use as your once-per-year/turn action choice.After initial production and a city or two are up and running, you will start terraforming via production of atmosphere, heat, etc. and this affects the regions' base temp, etc. Equator regions start off almost not-freezing, and the poles start off deadly cold. This affects comfort of cities, and which species of bacteria/plant/animal you can introduce to those regions.Hopefully you get the picture, there is a lot to do here already. There is meta-progress, where you unlock some of the more complex buildings/leaders as you finish games, and higher difficulty levels, where the game not only gets harder, but also longer.

candidates.title: Terraformers review
candidates.text: Terraformers is another new Martian colonisation game that is closer to the digital boardgame Terraforming Mars than it is Surviving Mars. I suppose you could call Terraformers a single player boardgame.I love games about Mars - I suspect I've played them all. I like them closer to real science than I do the more imaginative Mars games, such as Per Aspera. I also prefer the more global focus of Terraformers over, say, Surviving Mars. In Terraformers you'll find yourself colonising the whole planet rather than a sector. It is then up to you whether you colonise the world or keep it in its pristine state...or at least as close as with all the mining you'll do.Terraformers is in early access, and it's on of those early access titles that is very playable from the get go - in case the words early access concern you. There's a fully developed roadmap that tantalises what is to come. Right now the game is easy to beat. I beta my first game today and didn't come close to losing. I was actually just setting up to really push terraforming when I suddenly won. I wanted to carry on but that is afeature to come.I got a nice unlockables window when I got to the victory screen. I hadn't realised that the game had this and it does mean that at this early stage there are reasons to keep playing.It is safe to say I am impressed with Terraformers so far. I can't wait to see the game develop. Afterall, I could colonise Mars every day.Now, if only I could actually go there!EDIT: I must add that is was only after going to start a new game that I realised it could get harder than my first go. I am now thinking your 'first game' is kind of an extended tutorial.

candidates.title: Terraformers review
candidates.text: but there's also more specialized scenarios where you have to specifically get to an objective (again terraforming, building many mines for every resource, etc).I adore board games, turn-based games, resource management, sci-fi, city builders, the game hits a lot of sweet spots and if this sounds like fun to you, I recommend it to you.I hope they keep adding new stuff, I'll gladly buy the supporter pack to get behind this project.If there is one thing that I would like to see is a little bit of variety in the early game buildings.

candidates.title: Misha Kiyama
candidates.text: Mishas ability to Import Lifeforms can easily Jumpstart the Terraforming process of Mars, since the first Bacteria Spreader is always automatically obtained when the first Bacterium is imported to mars, allowing a head start for bacteriums which raise the temperature or the levels in atmosphere and oxygen. Since early Terraforming can be majorly impacted by the fast spread of bacteria, building multiple bacteria spreaders is a feasable strategy, which is greatly supported by the Specialization. Unfortunately the late game Impact of the Specialization is negligable, since it the bacteria spreaders become nearly obsolete, once the terraforming milestones are reached.

candidates.title: Terraformers review
candidates.text: Ein Strategiespiel dass es sich zur Aufgabe macht eine mögliche Geschichte zu erzählen wie der Mars besiedelt werden könnte. Für ein Early-Access Titel hat es schon einige besondere Features wo jedoch hoffentlich noch andere dazukommen werden. Der einstig in das Spiel ist auch schön gestaltet, man wird nicht mit einer Wucht an Informationen überflutet sondern lernt alle nötigen Infos schritt für schritt und der Anstieg der Komplexität ist genau richtig.Ich würde mir nur wünschen es würde einen größeren unterschied machen welche Spielweiße man wählt. Das Terraforming hat mir zu wenig Einfluss auf die Stats, ich finde auch das die steigende Unzufriedenheit unbelohnend ist, es gibt z.b. keine Möglichkeit die Marsmüdigkeit, trotz noch so viel ähnlichkeit des Marses zur Erde, zu senken. Klar braucht das Spiel auch im späteren Spielverlauf einen Challengefaktor. Aber es sollte meiner Meinung nicht mehr an der Zufriedenheit sondern durch einen neun Faktor wie z.b. an Umweltverschmutzung, Energieknappheit, Nahrungsversorgung die Challenge ins Game kommen. Ebenso ist es unsatisfying dass man den Mars in den Challanges nie bis zum Ende Terraformt, es reicht meist aus 1/5 davon zu Terraformen, oft kommt es auch in den schwierigsten Schwierigkeitsgraden vor dass man gar nicht dazu kommt überhaupt zu beginnen die Fauna zu verteilen, da man schin zuvor gewonnen hat. Das alles sind aber normale Kritikpunkte eines Early-Access Titels und ich bin gespannt was der Entwickler noch daraus zaubern wird.

candidates.title: Terraformers review
candidates.text: Good for an early access game, but there are several frustrating mechanics. 1 is the happiness mechanic, sometimes you just don't get the cards that can boost the happiness leading to an early loss even if you are doing great elsewhere.2 is the ocean level, only being able to increase ocean level by extraction and space project is very annoying. There are several times where I just couldn't get the space project to get the ocean level high enough, causing a green path loss. 3. each round you pick 1 out of 3 potential cards with buildings to give more. I think it should be 1 out of 4 or 5 as the default to reduce the luck involved in the game.

candidates.title: Terraformers review
candidates.text: Terraformers is a great game: intellectually engaging, beautiful, fun, and fluid gameplay.I wouldn't call the game "rogue-like" per se simply because of the random cards and resources; it's a solid resource management game.The only mixed feelings I have about the game is about the difficulty levels - the difficulty ramps quite quickly; the hardest levels are indeed hard, so should provide adequate level of challenge. But the challenge seems to come from two sources: - faster and more brutal penalties from macro factors (pop expectation levels, comfort levels, disasters) - the deck of cards become larger and larger as you progress-> I think the second point is an issue. The mechanics are: as you complete the easier scenarios, you get achievement points that unlock new cards. The problem is that not all new cards are superior than initial cards: some of them are and complement the game nicely (eg building stuff on ocean titles), but others are simply more expensive cards that generate more output (eg the 30+ resource cards). Therefore, at the more challenging levels, you end up have to build your economy and support much faster AND have a lower probability of receiving initial cards that are balanced and needed (eg all the basic +1 resource cards).This is only my hunch by reading the game mechanics; if that is true, this makes the game challenging for a bit frustrating reasons (why am I getting these super expensive cards at the beginning of the game).I'm still playing, so let's see how it progresses. But I'm still having lots of fun w it, so definitely recommend.

candidates.title: Terraformers review
candidates.text: While Terraformers of Mars has a hopeful, period aesthetic and the game play on non-achievement scenarios is enjoyable... the fiendishly contrived negative support meter thwarts good choices, good resource management and even leadership picks. This makes for a doomed experience for most I imagine, it's actually quite disheartening and (unless you just play this as a clicker in the non achievement mode) it's not a source of enjoyment, quite the opposite despite the initial promise. -Steven

candidates.title: Terraformers review

candidates.title: May devlog: Updates since EA, and a look at what we are working on
candidates.text:
We have now shifted our focus towards work on future updates, following our roadmap and specific improvements requested by the players. The features that are planned for the first major Early access update are:

Technologies
Technologies are the aspect of the update that will have the most impact on the gameplay. They are proposed like projects, but only cost science. A technology provides a global benefit that will allow you to specialize your strategy further. Some examples of benefits that technologies can give:

- Artificial intelligence: New robots provide +1 support income
- Enhanced Photosynthesis: Newly planted trees produce double the oxygen and gas.
- Megastructure Construction: When constructing a building that costs at least 40 resources, gain 5 random resources back.

Example of upcoming technology project.

Marsyclopedia
We will also add the first iteration of a “Marsyclopedia” to the main menu. Here, you will find all projects, lifeforms, leaders and locations that you’ve encountered at least once in the game. You can read up on them here and have a good overview, which can help you get a better understanding of the different potential strategies in the game.

Design conceprt of the Marsyclopedia screen.

Custom Mode
This might be our most requested feature since the launch, so we’ve decided to include it in the first major update as well. In custom mode, you’ll be able to set up the game to exactly how you want it by defining the victory condition, expectation rise frequency and severity of damage you’ll receive during the game. You can even choose not to select a victory condition and fully remove expectation rises and damage, allowing you to play a stress-free endless sandbox version of the game. Some mechanics might not hold up in very long runs, but it will be part of the Early Access journey to discover and address that together.

Custom mode screen, you can set it to be “endless”.

More improvements for future EA updates

candidates.title: Sim Companies review
candidates.text: If you're a fan of economy and market simulation games, this is a must-play. You have the flexibility to engage with it actively by spending a few hours managing the market and trading, or you can take a more passive approach by checking in once every 24 hours to list your items on the market or restock your stores.This game offers a true economy simulation experience, allowing you to produce various items that other players will use to create more products, which they'll then sell to retailers who, in turn, sell to NPCs. Despite the complexity of these interactions, the game is surprisingly accessible. While you can dive into it with a highly analytical mindset if you choose, it's not necessary.If any of this piques your interest, I highly recommend giving it a try.

candidates.text: 商业游戏评论：《Sim Companies》——商业模拟的真实挑战引言在众多商业模拟类游戏中，《Sim Companies》凭借其真实的经济机制和战略深度，吸引了无数玩家的关注。 作为一款在线多人商业模拟游戏，它允许玩家在一个虚拟的市场中创造、管理和发展自己的公司。 本文将探讨《Sim Companies》的核心玩法、经济机制、社区互动及其独特魅力。 游戏玩法《Sim Companies》让玩家从创建公司开始，选择不同的行业和产品。 玩家可以选择生产消费品、重工业、科技产品等，甚至可以选择开设零售店。 游戏的核心在于资源管理和市场竞争，玩家必须根据市场需求变化调整生产线，优化供应链，以确保公司的盈利。 在游戏中，玩家需要通过市场研究和数据分析来了解消费者的需求和市场趋势。 这种策略性思维不仅增加了游戏的深度，也使玩家能够体验到商业决策的复杂性。 每一个选择都会影响公司的成长和市场地位，玩家必须谨慎考虑，以避免陷入财务危机。 经济机制《Sim Companies》的经济系统设计非常真实，模拟了实际商业环境中的竞争与合作。 玩家之间的交易、合作与竞争使得市场充满活力。 通过建立合资企业、共享资源和进行市场交易，玩家可以影响市场供需关系，进而提升自己的市场份额。 此外，游戏还引入了经济波动的机制，玩家要时刻关注市场动态，及时调整策略。 例如，原材料价格的波动、竞争对手的崛起，都会对公司的运营产生重大影响。 这种经济机制的设计，使得游戏不仅仅是简单的生产和销售，更是一个需要深思虑的战略游戏。 社区互动《Sim Companies》拥有一个活跃的在线社区，玩家可以在游戏内外进行交流、合作和竞争。 社区活动和赛事为玩家提供了展示自己商业才能的舞台，激励玩家不断优化自己的公司管理。 此外，玩家间的互动也增加了游戏的趣味性，合作与竞争交织，使得每次游戏体验都独一无二。
