candidates.title: Warhammer 40,000: Darktide review
candidates.text: TLDR: Warhammer 40,000: Darktide is a fun and engaging game with great gameplay and atmosphere, but it is marred by an abundance of bugs and poorly implemented progression mechanics. The lack of a story and the release of the game before it was fully developed with missing mechanics are also major drawbacks. Fat Shark, the developer, has repeated the same mistakes from their previous games like Vermintide and Vermintide 2, which is disappointing.Regarding the gameplay, players and I have praised the game for its fast-paced and satisfying combat, as well as the variety of weapons and enemies available. The atmosphere of the game is also noteworthy, with a convincing portrayal of the grim and gritty Warhammer 40,000 universe.However, many players (which i am a part of) have reported a high number of bugs, such as crashes, glitches, and broken achievements. Some players have also experienced problems with the matchmaking system, making it difficult to find a stable game.The progression mechanics have also been criticized. For example, the lack of a clear leveling system makes it difficult to track character progress, and the gear system is confusing and not well-explained. Additionally, the game has a lack of story which is a major drawback for players who look for a good narrative experience.Lastly, the game has been criticized for being released too early, with many missing mechanics that are supposed to be included. This is particularly disappointing for fans of Fat Shark's previous games, Vermintide and Vermintide 2, as the developer seems to have repeated the same mistakes in terms of release timing and missing features.Overall, while Warhammer 40,000: Darktide has a lot of positive aspects, the game is flawed by a high number of bugs and poorly implemented progression mechanics, which detract from the overall experience.

candidates.title: OCTOPATH TRAVELER II review
candidates.text: Rating 8/10The music is good. The combat system is good. Building characters feels somewhat meaningful. The visuals are good, the game blurs things in the distance too much though. The character stories are all not bad. Some are better than others. My biggest disappointment with the game is that the characters do not interact with each other enough. All of their stories are completely separate and in the context of the character stories, other characters are just there for combat. You could complete one character's story without ever getting another character, the only thing that would hold you back is combat. Crossed path stories exist, there are 4 of them that pair 2 characters into a story. They are nice but short, only around 2-4 hours to complete the entire story. There are small banter scenes that characters can have with each other. It's just banter though and all it may do is build some character.Endgame spoilers below......At the end of the game you finally get to see all of the characters interacting with each other, and the final boss eventually has you controlling all 8 characters in 2 parties of 4. The end of the game was my favorite part. If Octopath traveler 3 is ever made, my one hope is that they design the game in a way that lets characters meaningfully interact with each other for most of the game. For example, to move onto chapter 2 in stories you must complete chapter 1 for all characters. Thus it would make sense for characters to appear in each other's stories.

candidates.title: Marvel's Midnight Suns review
candidates.text: After playing for 77 hours in 1 week and beating the game once, I believe this is a MUST PLAY game for anyone interested in simple yet deep deck building, incredibly unique and engaging tactical combat. If you're a marvel fan and are looking for a marvel game but don't like tactical combat, this game probably isn't for you. This isn't a real time action game and you must be able to accept that it's a turn based game.I will review every part of the game starting from what is best and ending with what is worst.Combat: 10 / 10 ; Hero Roster: 10 / 10 ; Game Audio: 10 / 10 ; Stable Gameplay 8 / 10: Attack Animations 8 / 10 ; Deck Building: 8 / 10 ; Writing 8 / 10 ; Balancing 7 / 10 ; Overall Graphics 6 / 10 ; Meta System: 7 / 10 ; Story: 6 / 10 ; Friendship System 6 / 10 ; Abbey Exploration 4 / 10It's important to understand there are five distinct parts of the game: Combat System, Story System (cutscenes and cinematics as well as idle conversations and optional character interactions), Meta System (deckbuilding / leveling up your heroes), Friendship System of building relationships with heroes (which ties directly into the Meta System) and Exploration System (Abbey Exploration). During missions you engage with the Combat System and during Story Missions you also have cutscenes to integrate the Story System. Otherwise, Combat is separate from the other systems. Outside of missions you interact with the remaining remaining systems in "The Abbey".While you are in the Abbey you move around using a 3rd person camera.

candidates.title: God of War review
candidates.text: And yet another example on why Steam needs to give us more options than "yes/no". God of War is a strange game, because as far as ports go, this is amazingly well done. A far cry from the dumpster-fire we were all anticipating from the jamokes at Sony Interactive. The thing about God of War is that it makes a great first impression. The presentation is rich, the combat functions without a hitch, and the overall world is overflowing with immense gravitas. In short, the game is well assembled. The art team, coders, modelers, etc all did their job and did them well.This is frustrating, because the core issue of the game really is just an endless parade of questionable design decisions. As many of you are aware, God of War tries for a new combat system that’s sort of akin to Dark Souls meets RE4. And RE4 is the comparison I find that I keep making, because the early issues with the game is that the game is extremely slow to dole out combat options. By the time I had the ability to do anything cool, I already had it ingrained in me to just safely stay back and continuously hucking axes until everything was dead, whether that was some green peon to a giant… uh…. Giant. Maybe I’d go into rage mode if I wanted to spice things up. And while it might be easy to simply say “well that’s your fault for playing like that”, the point is that the game (at least six hours in) does very little to incentivize you to utilize your full kit. Speaking of slow, pacing is also a rather irritating aspect of the game. Like many modern AAA, this one tries to go for a small, open world, seemingly for the sake of padding the runtime by forcing the player to backtrack (It’d be nice if the world was interesting enough to justify exploration for its own sake).

candidates.title: Warhammer 40,000: Darktide review
candidates.text: Darktide launched incomplete. I don't know why, but it was clearly not a finished game when it came out - from the lack of crafting, to the extremely limited skill trees, to the regular crashing and optimization issues, it was clear Darktide launched too soon, and it's overall rating reflects thatSo, a little over a year later, is it complete?At this point, it's probably as complete as Vermintide 1 was when it launched. So...no, it's not complete. But it IS whole. There's nothing significant that needs to be fixed or modified. It's incomplete in the sense that there's a lot more that's going to be added to the game from here on out. Or at least, that's what this developer's history would suggest to me. But we are at(or past) the point at which the game have launchedThere is a very solid core of fun gameplay here, built off the Vermintide system, but with significant changes to the ranged combat(both player and enemy). I wouldn't call Darktide's system an improvement on Vermintide's system so much as a pivot down a different direction.The melee gameplay is similar to Vermintide, which is to say, good. There are some differences(you can slide now - wheeee sliding), but for the most part the actual 'using weapons to bonk enemies' gameplay is unchangedThe ranged combat is in a good place. Ranged weapons are lethal, sound cool, and feel weighty.And the game great. All of the levels look good, the enemies are striking and memorable, the visuals on pretty much all the weapons are fantastic.The talents are well laid out, and none of the upgrade nodes really feel like insignificant upgrades.

candidates.title: OMORI review
candidates.text: This is another one of those situations where Steam really needs a "Neutral" or "Mixed" Review option. I enjoyed my time with this game overall, but it has some serious issues that makes me hesitant to recommend it at all.On the one hand, the last two hours or so is some of the most beautifully executed storytelling I've ever experienced. I have never had a game ending affect me so strongly emotionally the way Omori has.On the other hand, I found the gameplay to be sorely lacking and it absolutely killed the pacing at points. The battle system seems interesting at first, but it's only superficial and is lacking a lot of depth. Bosses have two or sometimes even one move they spam over and over with no variation and normal encounters feel borderline pointless.Even outside of the boring combat, most NPC interactions and 'puzzles' feel like chores and are quirky for the sake of being quirky. There are plenty of good moments and the writing and characterisation is solid throughout, especially in the non-headspace parts of the game, but these moments are broken up by hours of tedium and boredom.If you don't mind wallowing through about 15-20 hours of shallow, forgettable filler then there's a great story here that I'd say is worth experiencing. Otherwise, I can't recommend it.

candidates.title: Wildermyth review
candidates.text: I love the concepts behind this game - but in many cases I find the actual implementation of these concepts lacking.What I liked:* The main premise of the game - the fact that characters change and evolve over time, in response to both combat and non-combat events - is definitely cool. And many of these changes have interesting combat implications.* I love how mages work in this game - it's novel, interesting, and adds a lot of interactivity to the combat arenas.* I love how in-combat death is handled! And it's actually a deeper system than it appears at first, with aspects like one character sacrificing themslves for another, permanent maiming, building graves for fallen characters, and more.* Catching spirits is fun :-)What I didn't like:* My number 1 complaint is that I find the dialogs tedious. Extremely tedious. They play a large and important role in this game - they are not just filler between combat missions - and they are often too long, too unclear, and in many cases, too vague and philosophical. It got to a point where I just wanted to skip them, which for this kind of game is a sign that I should probably stop playing.* And in addition, for me, the dialogs didn't really convey consistent character personality; and I didn't perceive any consistent character relationship with the exception of the explicit relationships you pick, which are few in number.* The combat difficulty progresses weirdly. I'd say a majority of the encounters were too easy, a small number extremely hard, and only for a small minority I felt they were truly challenging but fair. Plus character progression significantly increases the power of each character, which means that new recruits typically provide relatively little value when added at a later chapter, making the difficulty curve even wonkier - encounters become cakewalk with too many veterans and impossible with too many newbies.* There are only 3 classes.

candidates.title: Phoenix Point review
candidates.text: Just a very underwhelming experience overall. The weapons don't feel powerful at all. The combat feels sluggish, even for an X-COM-like game, and the turn system is far too rewarding. Very little is explained about the games deeper mechanics and it's a lot less visually aesthetic when compared to other X-COM games, even when compared to X-COM UFO Defence. This game just feels very bland and generic. It has potential, sure. But that potential is buried deep under a pile of confusion, identity crisis, and a storyline that does very little to try and win me over. Just generic characters, fighting in a generic setting, with bland voicelines and underwhelming firepower. P.S. And it doesn't help that even after a full year of EPIC store exclusivity, this game still feels unfinished and bland.

candidates.title: Hades review
candidates.text: Man, I am really conflicted on this one. I really want to like this game. From a technical and aesthetical viewpoint this game is absolutely great. Runs smooth with no bugs other than a few minuscule visual ones. The story is really good with interesting characters and a ton of voice acting. However, the more I played the more I got annoyed by the combat and progression system. The first areas play very well, and thats where I have the most fun. But then it turns more and more into a bullet hell with spongy enemies. The screen gets clouded in explosions and particles which makes it really hard to impossible to tell what is going on. That compared with the environment that is sometimes blocking the view, especially around the walls at the bottom makes fighting really not fun. What I also don't like is how you receive damage. It is possible to get constant chip damage with no reliable way of dodging it. I think if would be better if the enemies hit harder, but less frequently. The thing that I don't like about the progression system is that it is build around playing the game to gather resources to make yourself permanently stronger. So you get farther every run, but not necessarily because you get better at the game, but because you made the game easier. You later get the option to make your runs more challenging to get extra rewards, but it's not a natural progression of the game. All in all it's a game with a great foundation but lacking game design, I personally didn't like the later gameplay, probably won't complete it.

candidates.title: DevBlog #2: New Unit System.
candidates.text:
This is the 2nd blog in our new series, which discusses developing our updated engine that will power the next title in the Grand Tactician-series. We're keeping some details, like historical setting, vague on purpose to discuss at a later stage. But, we’ll keep releasing these peeks behind the scenes to let you know what to expect in terms of game play and improvements.

The New Unit System

One of the first things we developed for The Civil War (during 2016-17) was what we call the Unit System. This is how units are created and handled in the battle layer, and it has a big impact on a multitude of other things: visuals, controls, performance, AI, to name a few.

Re-building the Unit System is a key part of improving the battle layer for the upcoming title. The results are very encouraging and we’re excited about the possibilities it brings to the table, both for game play and also for performance and clunkiness (or lack of, this time around) of the battles. This will of course work hand-in-hand with terrain and movement, group-system, combat system(s), AI, and so on.

The Old System

In the old system, we built the units from what we call “company blocks”. These are sub-elements of the units, and platforms, that are moved depending on the unit’s formation and positioning. The 3D models (or as the game originally featured, sprite soldiers!) are attached to each platform.

candidates.title: Expeditions: Rome review
candidates.text: I wanted to like this game but it's repetitive. Stalled out on wanting to play more. Most of the game honestly feels like a chore on the campaign map/army battles. Each new region is just the same but reskinned basically. Fighting the same unit comp with different skins. The combat system is ok but get's pretty dull. I don't know what I was expecting with this game, but this wasn't it. The world feels small despite it's supposed big scale. The combat system feels like just rolling the dice to get a new skin and some lazy narrative as to why you are fighting it. No decisions on the campaign map felt impactful. Answering them just led to the same result anyways.Almost seems like the creators spent a lot of time on the combat system. Copy and pasted each battle throughout the entire game, and then rushed some overarching narrative as to why you're even fighting at all. If the devs seriously take into consideration the negative reviews, maybe the next title in this genre will be better.

candidates.title: Black Myth: Wukong review
candidates.text: The graphics are stunning, and the map looks great. However, the map design itself is a complete mess, cluttered and lacking in distinctiveness. Coupled with the numerous and unreasonable invisible walls, it's hard not to think that this is all just for the sake of the visuals and art—a case of style over substance.The boss design feels uneven. Some monsters are satisfying to fight against, while others are just plain annoying. Either their hit boxes are weird, or the bosses have irritating moves. In soul-like games, they are tough, but you can find tricks and rhythms to gradually conquer them. However, the bosses in this game seem to rely on luck: the hit boxes are terrible, I dodge but somehow still get hit by the boss. There are various unreasonable jumping slashes and attack patterns that feel like they're locked in. Then there's the stitched-together combat system: the protagonist has a mana bar, extremely long cooldowns for skills, a stamina bar, perfect dodge, charge attacks, non-cancellable heavy attacks, very slow light attacks, and no defense... Fighting bosses feels like it's just for the sake of progressing through the game, most of them aren't enjoyable.The mana bar and extremely long cooldowns make it frustrating when you misuse a spell; the stamina bar means you have to rest a bit after a combo when fighting bosses; the very slow basic attacks (both light and heavy, plus the charge bar) don't give you the exhilarating, mindless slashing satisfaction found in games like God of War because there's no defense, and you constantly have to watch out for running out of energy and sudden counterattacks from enemies. The whole combat system feels pieced together and lacks a cohesive system.

candidates.title: February Content Update
candidates.text:
We're very aware that we've been creeping up in performance requirements lately and so this update we did a bit of spring cleaning early! We've boosted FPS and lowered CPU usage across the board by optimization in dialog cameras, NPCs roaming around the world, textures, particles and more!

We're always working on continually improving the performance in the game and we're currently prototyping some much more radical changes.

Combat

We've changed our targeting system, moving back to our previous system with dynamic targeting. We felt that managing two combat targeting systems(which is what we had) ended up being messy and not what we intended; now we're focusing on polishing and making one system. Additionally, a change some of you will notice is that thrust attack is now sprint + regular attack rather than having it's own keybind.

We're currently working on incorporating magic into the combat system this will be coming later this year with it's own quest. Ranged upgrades and improvements are also on the way with bow crafting, arrows and some changes to enemy behavior.

Squish goes the Bug

We've tried our best to go through as many bugs we could find in the update and fix as many as we can in time for the update, including issues with Milk and Honey, Quest tracking, day/night issues, fast travel, NPCs, animations, typos, save/load issues and more! Check out the full change log below and we hope you now have a smoother experience all round!

candidates.title: OCTOPATH TRAVELER II review
candidates.text: Review in short:"Astonishing visuals and a good combat system crippled by a massive ludo-narrative dissonance, story inconsistencies and issues with enemies scaling."Intro info on how I played:* Played on PC with controller* Played in japanese sub engPro:+ Astonishing visuals+ Really good OSTs+ Stories with adult themes accessible for a younger audience, although sometimes said themes are treated with too much naivety+ Really good voice acting+ Interesting combat mechanics+ Visible turn order and how it changes with certain actions+ Not all chapters are battle-related+ Good visual hints for secrets+ Party banters+ Side-stories with character pairs (although it's only a small amount)+ Fast travel from everywhere+ Day/Night mechanics+ Possibility to remap controlsCons:- Save game is possible only at save points- No difficulty selection- Too many random encounters- Description of companions or summons abilities is not available in battle, only their name- No Flee confirmation- Cannot change the party in battle or in the over-world, but only at taverns- No party interactions or reactions to certain actions (such as stealing)- No dialogues log- Too much redundancy and overlapping in characters' out-of-combat abilities- Cannot remove from the party the character chosen to start the game, making them always over-leveled as only characters on the field gain exp- Severe issues with the management of enemy levels in areas and story chapters; too much disparity throughout the game.- No character influence or even just presence in each others' story chapters, even when it would make sense.

candidates.title: Hardspace: Shipbreaker review
candidates.text: This game is an acquired taste, personally I like these kind of games. You may or may not develop one though; if you already have such a taste, go ahead. Otherwise, I'd give a neutral recommendation, however, the recent (and apparently the biggest) 0.4.0 update has been a huge disappointment for me, and if this is how things are going to be, the future of the game doesn't look great to me. And that's why I'm going to pick no. Let me elaborate. On / after the previous 0.3.0 update & 0.3.1 hotfix (which was around 4-5 months ago as of writing this), developers have stated that they'll be releasing fewer but bigger updates, which I'm entirely cool with. Seeing a new update, and how the developers stating that this is the biggest one yet, I was hoping to see new hull types, tools, tool upgrades, etc... content so to speak. And the keyword there is content.The main catch for me in a game like this, as the game title suggests, and as it is highly specific in what it does, is breaking ships apart. And content for me in this game is based mainly on how many distinct ship hulls there are, how many tools I can use, and how many upgrades I can purchase. The 0.4.0 update; the biggest update yet did nothing on these three main things I consider content in this game, unfortunately. There is a new ship type in the said update, and more variations on ships, but these don't add much for me; they still use the same ship hulls, and there's just three hull types. On the side, the progression overhaul just dilutes what little content there is with an extremely grindy, time-consuming fashion. As there are just three hull types, you'll be cutting the same things over and over to a point that you might get bored out of your skull as there will probably be nothing exciting / new for a long while.

candidates.title: UNCHARTED™: Legacy of Thieves Collection review
candidates.text: I didn't get a single minute of gameplay. You could tell me any possible solution, and I can almost guarantee I tried it. I went completely insane. Over four days, the average time I spent troubleshooting was a little under two hours per day. That’s seven and a half hours of pure opening and closing the game. I practically had given my PC a complete wipe. I reduced the storage by at least twenty five percent from uninstalling apps and software. I reinstalled my drivers about eight times. I did everything humanely possible. I paid for a game, that I wanted to enjoy, but instead, I received nearly eight hours of pure torment and insanity. Thank you Iron Galaxy for PTSD of the beginning credits of this game.

candidates.title: Teardown review

First mission and I destroyed the whole ground floor and walls and expected the building to topple, which it would in real life with not supporting structure. Stopped playing. Came back to it once release 1.0, was here. Same issue on 1st mission. Bad physics. Was expecting something like Red Faction Guerrilla but better. I know I haven't played long but if the first mission cannot get the physics right, what's the point in playing. I have already bought this game but hopefully this review will help those who intend to purchase and do not waste their money if they are expecting a physics based game. Looks nice though.

candidates.title: Hardspace: Shipbreaker review
candidates.text: As there are just three hull types, you'll be cutting the same things over and over to a point that you might get bored out of your skull as there will probably be nothing exciting / new for a long while. Combined with (what I consider to be) no new meaningful content, you'll be stuck on a smaller portion of the game for longer. You might see my biggest issue with this update now, I believe. A big update doesn't necessitate new content, but as a gamer, that's what I expect to be honest. And right now, the game needs more content; more ship hulls, tools, tool upgrades, and so on. However, what 0.4.0 did for me was a content rehash with slower progression, and nothing else. That's why I said "the future of the game doesn't look great for me, if this is how things are going to be". We'll see in time I guess.I'll definitely review my... review on the next update. But for now, as I've said, if you already have taste or itch, go for it. Otherwise, I'd say follow the game, and decide on the next update. As sad as it makes me, I have to go with a no for now unfortunately.

candidates.title: Eternal Return review
candidates.text: I was introduced to this game at Dreamhack, but the matching queues are absolutely terrible playing in PvP. You have what looks like bots (I can't believe any human player would be this stupid) and 6 season veterans in the same queue where a newbie has absolutely no chance. The queue wait times are very long (>10 mins) for solo, and it feels unrewarding to spend 3-4 minutes collecting and get pounced on by a veteran and dead in 15 seconds or less. You don't learn anything with such a low PvP vs PvE interaction.I think I may return if MMR balancing was better (and I mean, Top 100 should not be queued with newbies) and a better tutorial system was implemented with timing feedback as the looting phase is a big issue. The main game mechanic issue that is singularly frustrating and is mentioned by others is the amount of time wasted in chase versus evade where engaging and disengaging seems extremely unfair for certain characters. On the positive side, the drops and progression seem reasonable, and the game is really free-to-play with IRL money for cosmetics and non-gaming accessories (announcer voice packs, emotes, etc.) which are both desirable but nonessential. The design makes you want to buy the loot, you don't need to buy the loot to progress.

candidates.title: Marvel's Midnight Suns review

candidates.title: Frostpunk 2 review
candidates.text: I truly recommend the game. I was a big fan of the first game (played it like 200h in a pirated version). But the first time when I heard the second game was being made I truly didn't give a ♥♥♥♥, yes I enjoyed the first one but I thought the second game will be frostpunk but with petrol, the same thing but a little different.When I saw the first trailer, my jaw dropped. I couldn't of imagined that they had the balls to do something this drastically different from the first one, while still truly fallowing the vision and narrative path of the first.The game is amazing in most that it is trying to do, and shows that it learned from the 'mishaps' of the first. The first game was centered around the main scenario, and for many the main scenario was the peak of the game, and for many the rest even if the rest of the scenarios were good, it didn't scratch the same itch, also the first game took a while to release the endless mode that also ended up being underwhelming, since after a while there would be nothing to do in such a scenario. The second game focused on the sandbox and endless mode, since unlike the first it isn't about the cost of survival but the cost of ambition. The main campaign is more like a tutorial for the player to understand all the components of the game and to go experiment and test themselves in the utopia builder mode. All the mechanics are also focused on the prolonging game, the laws can be signed, unsigned and changed unlike the rigid one in the first game, all resources are limited(with few and negligible exceptions) and the population increases to a staggering amount and all this people form under ideological believes and enter in conflicts among themselves.The first game was about surviving the end of the world, a great challenge which after beaten left nothing to do in that game.

candidates.title: Frostpunk 2 review
candidates.text: Let me start by saying if you are looking for Frostpunk 1 with updates: YOU WILL NOT FIND IT HEREFrostpunk 2 is an "evolution" of the original in the truest sense of the word. The question of "how do a group of stranglers survive the collapse of the word and the oncoming frost?" have been thoroughly answered by the first the game. The humanity defining conflicts that were so difficult to make every time you made them, are now a common occurrence. Where in the first game you could try your hardest to hold on to what little there was to hold on to of sanity and morals, NOW, after 30 years, those decisions are now monthly, or weekly, or even daily. A group barely surviving the frost, now desires to conqueror it, tired of barely surviving.The mechanics of everything have been changed, overhauled, and streamlined from the first game, turning in it to the scale operation needed. But the heart and character of frostpunk, "humanity vs the frost" that is told with so much love, is told all the better here.

candidates.title: Frostpunk 2 review
candidates.text: A true evolution from frostpunk 1. The game scales up in almost every way you could imagine, more people, time moves faster, bigger problems, bigger buildings, and a bigger city. candidates.title: Frostpunk 2 review
candidates.text: Let me make it clear from the start. Frostpunk 2 is a completely different game than Frostpunk 1 and I commend the developers for this bold step.In Frostpunk 1 you had to build your city from the start, placing each individual building and assigning each individual worker to beat the inevitable storm that is quickly approaching. In Fropstunk 2 you are past that initial survival setup and start expanding outwards by placing districts and assigning workforces to each district.The core concept of both games is the same, yet the games are different enough to enjoy both as different games.11 bit studios is one of the few developers who actually do listen to the games. Yes, not all games are happy with the direction they take, but it is ultimately their choice and there is now way they can satisfy every gamer.The request that could not be implemented in Frostpunk 1, was addressed in Frostpunk 2. Examples of this to name a few is:You can now build coloniesThe law tree is not fixed anymore and can be changed as you see fitResearch tree increased exponentially and not blocking other options that was disregarded. Only the generator upgrade choice is fixed. The game play is still the same as in Frostpunk 1 where it is your city vs the Storm, but it is way more complicated.

candidates.title: Frostpunk 2 review
candidates.text: I had been somewhat dreading my own experience with this game because I had seen the advertisements and early reviews claiming how different Frostpunk 2 is to the first game. And while this is true, the real question is if these changes are for the better? I'd say its pretty subjective.In terms of tone, Frostpunk 2 is very different from its predecessor. In the first game, there was this constant eldritch horror of being at the mercy of the elements, with several hundred survivors huddled around a generator, building to distract themselves from the reality of 90% of humanity being wiped out by an apocalyptic natural disaster. In the sequel, this tone has been replaced with a dreadful sense of never ending tension and feeling constantly short-handed by the various factions and preventing them (and yourself, Steward) from going to extremes too quickly. And this is understandable because the scope of the game is bigger and you have multiple settlements and colonies to manage on top of your main city. If Frostpunk 1 was about several hundred survivors trying to build a post-apocalyptic community, Frostpunk 2 is about managing several communities to build the foundation of a post-apocalyptic nation.The social management aspect of Frostpunk 2 is where most of the action in the game lies, which probably explains why the economic systems of this game remain relatively simple (and time management honestly matters less compared to the first game). It is the constant tension between factions that will drain your heatstamps and drain your resources more than any natural disaster in Frostpunk 2. And this is probably what makes the learning curve of Frostpunk 2 harder than its predecessor because even at the lowest difficulty, things can fall apart very quickly unless you want to turn into a dictator or just favour one faction from the get go.I really want to like this game, I do appreciate the thought and care put into building on the foundations of the first game to create something new.

candidates.title: Frostpunk 2 review
candidates.text: Frostpunk 2 is a good game and worth buying, but there are a lot of pros and cons to it. The community seems divided over it being both too similar, and too different from Frostpunk 1 at the same time. FP2 is same in the ways it functions, you place buildings, get resources, and make crucial decisions to quell unrest. Its also the same, if not better, in terms of atmosphere. The sound and graphic design are really good, city wide announcements like "Citizens, please make way for frostbreaking teams in transit" add a surprising amount of satisfaction in ambience, and the music is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ unbelievably good, much like the first game.The problem arises with the scale of FP2. The magic of FP1 was racing against the clock, knowing your small settlement had to absolutely haul ass in order to survive -200C storms. Every. Decision. Mattered. This game has that to a degree, but not nearly as much. Resources are more complicated, the UI is not as easy to read, and the city is more zoomed out, with reduced intimacy with your citizens. It is overall harder to understand how much your citizens are fighting for survival, how successful you are managing things, and is less satisfying when you pull off a difficult maneuver.This makes absolute sense logically, the city is massive after all. But is it worth it? If you want the experience of Frostpunk, but haven't played the first game, I recommend getting FP1. Its one of the best games ever made imo. But if you've played FP1, this is an excellent successor with a lot of heart put into it. Unfortunately the devs had the near impossible task of making a sequel to what was essentially a perfect game. That being said, in the 6 years since FP1, I would've really liked to see more large gameplay mechanics added.

candidates.title: Frostpunk 2 review
candidates.text: There are other, more detailed comments that describe my problem with the game quite fittingly. But i want to summarize the main points for myself:Totally different compared to the first game and overall, i think that's a great idea. The setting is amazing and to approach the setting and story with a different gameplay is sooo much better than to just do the same again. Sadly the new approach didn't work for me very well, because: - The city building feels kinda boring and i can't really get the feeling of it being MY precious city (mainly because you only really see the districts that are planted and all the different special addon buildings are not worth mentioning)- Differences between the special buildings of the different factions are totally irrelevant... bit more workers, bit more output, bit more heat... that's all there is to it) --> i think there was to much focus on the really good politic system and the differences there - Campaign was fun, but so much less compared to the first game. There you had different settings, different objectives on different maps... here you just stay at the same point and if you play slow you are so strong at around chapter 2 or 3 that you can finish the rest of the chapters in 30min I really hope that the add-ons and patches bring more stuff to the campaign and more differences between the special add-on buildings (optical and mechanic)... but at the moment there isn't enough content/fun for me to recommend it.

candidates.title: Frostpunk 2 review
candidates.text: As with the first game: I highly recommend.While the scale may be larger, Frostpunk 2 is still very much a Frostpunk game. While you may not place individual buildings anymore, the core of what makes Frostpunk: Managing resources, both human and more mundane, prioritisation, and the ever present feeling of desperation (And the hard choices that come with it), are all present and better than ever. Do you focus on getting a roof ever everyone's head, or do you ensure they are fed first? Do you put off manufacturing goods to ensure you're making the maximum heat credits, or accept the loss to ensure you keep the deathcount as low as possible? I also think the political system added on top only enhances Frostpunk's strengths, and adds even more depth and choice to a playthrough.And at the end of the day, while the game is hard, it is fair. If you are good enough, you can even minimise how many hard choices you have to make.Phenomenal game. Cannot recommend enough.

candidates.title: Frostpunk 2 review
candidates.text: Frostpunk 2 is an excellent evolution of the first game through both gameplay and themes while retaining the core ideas that made the original special.Gameplay:This is still your gruelingly difficult steampunk cold fighting city builder game - but at a level higher than in the previous game. Instead of micro-managing a workforce of a few hundred, you are in charge of thousands organizing workforces of hundreds through districts. Furthermore, you can expand the interests of New London to new locations. The game has a clear influence on some of the mechanics introduced in the "On the Edge" DLC from the first game. Logistics is everything. Ensure there is enough housing. Ensure your new districts dont overwhelm your heat demand. Ensure your new population is fed. Ensure your buildings are being maintained.Along with this, the tech tree is now split on ideas by the factions you will encounter. Each have some interesting benefits or setbacks that have their appeal. Some techs will require a law to be introduced and passed by the council.The council is able to pass laws that attend to issues in the city, though you do not have the same authority as in the first game. A bill can be proposed as a law, and depending on the different delegates' worldviews, it will or wont go through. Some of the laws that need to be researched first can be a bit out of the way, or rarely encountered and is one of the main criticisms I have for this mechanic.I find it hard to believe that it takes about the same amount of time for my researchers to understand machinery used to recycle heat as it does the idea for privatized alcohol.Sound Design and Music:Much of the appeal of the first game comes from its presentation in sound and music, and that carries over the the second game. The light groaning of the generator in the first game has been replaced by intimidating sounds of machinery that echoes through the much larger city.

candidates.title: Frostpunk 2 review
candidates.text: O primeiro jogo te prende pela história, pelas decisões, pela dificuldade, mas aqui as coisas são... diferentes.Pessoas: O primeiro jogo você tem q se preocupar com cada pessoa pois uma a mais ou a menos é uma estrutura funcionando de forma reduzida e impactando toda a cidade, aqui no capítulo 2 você tem milhares e meio que tanto faz quem é quem, o que importa é os números.Frio: O principal elemento do jogo, no primeiro jogo não basta ter carvão, você vê na barrinha que em 2 dias vai esfriar 20 graus e você tem se virar pra proteger o povo, pesquise, construa estruturas, melhore edifícios, o frio te amedronta. Aqui o frio vai apenas gastar mais carvão, que vai fazer você ter que coletar mais carvão, e pra isso precisa de mais construções, mais comida, mais equipamento... Ficou tudo muito mais "gamificado".Dificuldade: O primeiro jogo tem uma dificuldade bem alta, a primeira vez que você joga cada mapa, você apenas apanha e acha que vai ser impossível ganhar o desafio, mas você continua jogando e vai percebendo que embora difícil, é possível. Já aqui parece que está muito mais artificial, pra conseguir vencer o primeiro mapa na dificuldade padrão fazendo as decisões "corretas" moralmente eu repeti umas 4x o mapa e foi no apagar das luzes, parece que o mapa foi planejado para você só conseguir vencer se fizer um passo-a-passo especifico pensado pelos devs.O jogo aqui tenta ter tantas coisas novas (muitas delas jogadas na sua cara de uma só vez aliás) que nem parece mais uma continuação, claro que só copiar e colar é muito fácil e não tem mérito nenhum, mas também precisamos manter coisas suficientes para não parecer outra coisa totalmente diferente, eu admiro a coragem dos desenvolvedores, mas ao mesmo tempo acho que eles poderiam ter dosado melhor.

candidates.title: Frostpunk 2 review
candidates.text: Frostpunk 2 is not - shocker - Frostpunk 1. It's a progression; a 'what if' wherein 30 years have passed since the first game and now it's time to try to do more than just hide from the ice in a hole. That hole isn't big enough anymore; there are thousands of people and more every day, and despite the storms coming in and wrecking everything exposed over and over, there literally isn't room to keep everyone in that little hole, and decisions have to be made.That's what Frostpunk 2 is about, in in many ways what it does share with the first game: decisions. In many ways I even feel it does decisions , because unlike the first game I have yet to find a situation where there is one best path that will see you through on the harder difficulties. In FP1, above certain difficulties you played a certain way or you lost. FP2, with its factional clashing preventing you from treading the exact path you planned, that isn't ven possible.The game is still beautiful - although I did find more visual impressiveness in the first. I hope desperately they at least add screenshot modes to 2 the way they did the first game.The narrative takes place at a bit more of a remove because, again, thousands of people rather than tens and hundreds. Interestingly though, I actually feel more immersed. In Frostpunk 1, the Captain was a nebulous individual who nudged the ant colony along particular lines. In 2... I'm a harried leader who people actually come to with demands, and who I have to bend to my intentions if I want to get anywhere. Do I want to use the moss-based air scrubbers because they work better and I only have so much space in my residential districts?

candidates.title: Age of Empires III: Definitive Edition review
candidates.text: Age of Empires III: Definitive Edition was supposed to be a grand return to form, a polished update of a classic RTS that once stood tall among its peers. But let’s be honest: it’s a bit of a letdown. Released in 2020, this "Definitive Edition" feels anything but. Instead of being a celebration of what made the original great, it’s more like a sluggish, clunky rehash that struggles to justify its existence in today's gaming landscape.First off, let’s talk about the graphics. It’s 2020 (well, 2024 now), and this game looks like it’s stuck in the early 2010s. Sure, the devs slapped on some new textures and called it a day, but honestly, it’s not enough. The visuals are inconsistent, with some units and buildings looking okay-ish, while others are painfully outdated. The environments, which should be immersive and detailed, instead feel flat and lifeless. For a game that's supposed to be definitive, it’s disappointing that it doesn't even look as good as some modern indie RTS games. It might have looked fine back in the day, but now it’s just plain underwhelming.Then there’s the gameplay. Age of Empires III always had its quirks, but those quirks now feel more like flaws in this definitive edition. The gameplay is clunky, and the controls feel unresponsive at times. Units sometimes don’t do what you tell them to, and managing large groups of them is more frustrating than it should be. Pathfinding issues that were a pain in the original still persist here, making you wonder what they actually improved in this edition.The pacing of the game is another issue. It’s slow. Like, painfully slow.

candidates.title: Age of Empires III: Definitive Edition review
candidates.text: Pathfinding issues that were a pain in the original still persist here, making you wonder what they actually improved in this edition.The pacing of the game is another issue. It’s slow. Like, painfully slow. In a genre where games like StarCraft II and even Age of Empires II: Definitive Edition manage to keep things engaging, Age of Empires III: DE feels like it’s dragging its feet. The AI isn't particularly challenging either, which makes single-player matches more of a slog than a strategic battle of wits.Okay, so what about the new content? They added some new civilizations and game modes, but it honestly feels like a thin layer of frosting on a stale cake. The new civs don’t do much to shake up the formula, and the historical battles are more of a chore than an exciting addition. It’s clear the developers tried to add some value, but these additions feel tacked on and don’t really address the underlying issues with the game.Multiplayer could’ve been this game’s saving grace, but nope, it’s just as frustrating. The matchmaking is slow, and there are still a bunch of bugs that can ruin matches. Lag spikes and disconnects are more common than they should be in a game that’s supposed to be a polished, definitive experience. And good luck trying to find a decently balanced match—half the time you’re either steamrolling or getting steamrolled.At the end of the day, Age of Empires III: Definitive Edition is a boring, clunky mess that doesn’t live up to its promise. It looks like it belongs in the past, and not in a nostalgic way, but in a “wow, games used to be this rough?” kind of way.

candidates.text: A very fun little game that is easy to learn but difficult to master. While some might compare it to "Getting Over It" the controls in Deepest Sword feel a lot better. You only use 4 keys in the game. One thing I didn't realize until I looked at the controls was that you could use the Arrow Keys instead of the mouse buttons, which is so much more convenient.If you don't have experience with speedrunning, this game is a great introduction. The mechanics are simple, you can easily find the skips that save time, and the runs are short enough that a mistake doesn't lose much progress. The fact that the developers have added in features to accommodate it are great, as well as the achievements to push you to complete it as quickly as possible.

candidates.title: Stoneshard review
candidates.text: 作为一个中世纪风格的游戏粉丝，我非常喜爱这款游戏，但还是有太多缺点需要制作组去完善。 我本想给予差评，但是我真心希望这款游戏能够进步，所以我还是决定留下好评并提出建议。 其实迅速提升玩家游戏体验的方法非常简单，先做到这三点：1.提供类似马匹、马车等交通工具帮助玩家在地图上移动，比如玩家能够骑马，加快在地图上移动的速度，并能在城镇中付钱来坐上马车由一座城市快速旅行到另一座城市。 再不济，模仿天国拯救的大地图快速移动方式也未尝不可。 我不明白为什么制作组要让玩家靠着双腿在地图上奔波，这是完全没有必要的。 2.添加即时存档功能。 我理解制作组想让游戏变得更加硬核，但完全不应该用限制存档这种手段，至少应该给予玩家选择，比如像骑马与砍杀那样的可选择的存档机制。 只能通过睡觉存档，这不是硬核，这是恶心玩家。 3.更新应该着力于扩大地图、增加可探索地点、增加更多职业和自定义职业的模式、完善游戏主线等，以此来提升游戏可玩性，而不是把精力放在过分夸张的“平衡”上。 As a medieval fan, I love the game, but there are still too many flaws for the production team to fix. I wanted to give it a bad review, but I really want the game to improve, so I decided to leave a good review and make suggestions. There are simple ways to quickly improve the player's experience. Provide transportation such as kingdomcome:deliverance to help the player move around the map. For example, the player can ride a horse, speed up the movement of the map, and pay for a carriage to travel quickly from one city to another in towns I don't understand why the production team would want players to run around the map on their legs, it's totally unnecessary 2.

New Menu Design: In-game menus are now more intuitive and easy to understand. From the main menu to trade options, we're providing a smoother navigation experience at every step.

Junkyard: A Realistic Vehicle Salvage Adventure

With the junkyard system, our goal is to provide players with a realistic car salvage and repair adventure. You'll buy real salvage vehicles from the junkyard and bring them back to life. However, a word of caution: we don't recommend buying every salvage vehicle! Some vehicles might have hard-to-find parts, requiring strategic thinking on your part.

Find Parts, Repair, and Get Back on the Road

Each salvage vehicle will have its unique set of parts. The process of repairing a car will begin once you've found the essential parts. Once these parts are correctly installed, the vehicle will become operational. But the process doesn't end there! Your vehicle might not be in the desired condition yet. question: What are the perks granted by the Badge of Restoration in God of War?

candidates.title: Multiplayer
candidates.text:
The powers of each warrior are displayed in the Stats list in the Multiplayer lobby. These Stats are:
Ascension Tokens: A new stat from the game's most recent update. Ascension Tokens can be acquired by reaching level 40 with any allegiance and then making the warriors "Ascension" with that allegiance. This causes the warrior to go back to the level 1 of that allegiance and lose the weapons and armors that are associated to it (except the Battle Armors, if they'd already been unlocked). Ascension Tokens can be used to buy the godly versions of armors and weapons. Skill Points: Acquired by upgrading the warrior from one level to another. Skill Points are used to upgrade Abilities (Magics, Items and Relics). The higher the level reached, the more Skill Points earned. The better the Ability is or the higher its level is, the more Skill Points required to upgrade it. Health: Health Points increase the warrior's health bar, allowing them to take more damage before dying. Health is the main focus of Poseidon. Elemental Power: Increases the damage of attacks that use elemental energy, such as Magics and some special attacks. Elemental Power is the main focus of Zeus. Elemental Resist: Increases the resistance to elemental damage. Physical Power: Increases the damage of physical attacks, such as the normal combos and some special attacks. Physical Damage is the main focus of Ares. Physical Resist: Increases the resistance to physical damage. Cooldown reduction: Reduces the time needed to "recharge" special attacks and Items after they are used, allowing players to use them again after a shorter period. Cooldown reduction is the main focus of Hades. Weapons and armors increase Stats.

candidates.title: Amulet of Yggdrasil
candidates.text:
Here you will find a list of the different Enchantments you can find and equip as you progress through the story, undertake side quests, and defeat optional bosses. There are six categories of Enchantments:

Realm Enchantments - These Enchantments normally focus only on improving Kratos' stats. But if you socket at least three of them, you'll unlock a Set Bonus Perk that will be increased based on one of Kratos' stats. There are five Enchantments for each of the nine realms.
Perk Enchantments - These don't give a stat bonus, and instead provide a Perk, similar to the rest of Kratos' gear. Many of these Perks won't activate until Kratos meets a minimum Stat value, making them useless otherwise.
Badge Enchantments - These New Game Plus-exclusive items replicate the Perks provided by the Shield Ronds from a standard playthrough. You buy them using Gilded Coins, which are awarded for upgrading a piece of gear to Power Level 9.1.
Engraving Enchantments - These New Game Plus-exclusive items are the same as Badge Enchantments, only they're based on Chest Armor Perks. These also require Kratos to meet a minimum Stat value before they'll activate, similar to Perk Enchantments.
Burden Enchantments - Exclusive to New Game Plus, these will inflict a negative buff on Kratos, making combat even more difficult.
Berserker Enchantments - Similar to Realm Enchantments, these New Game Plus-exclusive Enchantments focus purely on improving Kratos' stats. Unlike Ream Enchantments, they do not have Set Bonus Perks.

candidates.title: Enchantments (Ragnarök)
candidates.text:
Badges are Enchantments which grant perks from select Shield Rönds, when slotted into the Amulet of Yggdrasil. Like Engravings, they cost Gilded Coins to craft them and do not stack with the Rönds their perks are derived from, but unlike Engravings, they don't have stat requirements, in order to use them.

Badge of DisruptionPerkElemental StormLow Luck chance to create an Elemental Storm when interrupting double Blue ring attacks (Double Tap L1) or Parrying.AcquisitionCraft: 3 Gilded CoinsDescription"Does not stack with the Rönd of Disruption."

Badge of AbsorptionPerkDefender's MomentumThe Permafrost, Immolation and Maelstrom skill gauges increase when Blocking or Parrying.AcquisitionCraft: 3 Gilded CoinsDescription"Does not stack with the Rönd of Absorption."

Badge of RestorationPerkRestoring ShieldOn taking damage, Kratos has a Luck chance to gain Defence and for his next Shield Strike (Double Tap L1) hit to restore Health. The chance increases with lower health.AcquisitionCraft: 3 Gilded CoinsDescription"Does not stack with the Rönd of Restoration."

candidates.text:

candidates.title: Draupnir Spear
candidates.text: The Spear remained in Kratos' possession when he was drawn to the blessed realm of Valhalla by the real Týr to help Kratos overcome his trauma and accept his position as a member of Freya's inter-realm council. As Kratos embarks, he is given the option to follow the path of the Spear, which enhances its chances of gaining new powerful perks and abilities. It along with his other weapons help Kratos throughout his journey in Valhalla, clearing the mind and Mastering thyself.

candidates.title: Medusa
candidates.text:
During the siege of Athens, she was given the title of Queen of the Gorgons. She and her race are among the armies of Ares, as it is known that Gorgons hated Athena. As Kratos progressed through the ruins of the city, he met Aphrodite, who commanded him to slay Medusa by decapitating her. The hissing Gorgon arose from the shadows and fought with Kratos, who eventually tore her head from her body with his bare hands. Pleased, Aphrodite granted the power of Medusa's Gaze to Kratos, who in turn used it to destroy a group of Minotaurs.

Medusa's existence had come to an end, leaving her sisters, Euryale and Stheno, to lead the race of Gorgons until Euryale's death at the hands of Kratos in God of War II. Since Stheno appears in God of War: Ascension, this would mean that Medusa was the second queen of the Gorgons, and not the first.

In the God of War: Ascension multiplayer it is revealed that the hero Perseus has killed Medusa with a godly blade that he recieved from Athena. The novel of God of War reveals that the series follows the traditional story of Hesiod; with Medusa being seduced by Poseidon, rather than being violated by the Sea God as told by Ovid.God of War (Novel), Chapter 7 Somehow, Medusa returned to life by the events of the series.

candidates.title: Hyperion
candidates.text: The ancient story of Hyperion being granted the "secret flame primeval" by his mother Gaia is told again by the Lexicon of Laconia. Like in God of War: Lost World, the Titan is once more stated to be the eldest of the male Titans, and his sister-wife Theia to be the eldest of Gaia's daughters.

candidates.title: Powers
candidates.text:
Regeneration is the powerful magical ability that allows a user to regenerate and heal both damaged and diseased bodily tissues and organs. In God of War II, Zeus had this power as, after being stabbed by Kratos with the Blade of Olympus, we saw him on Olympus completely unharmed. Also, in God of War III, Gaia is seen to lose her left hand after Kratos cuts it off, but at the end of the game, when she confronts both Kratos and Zeus, her hand is regenerated in what seems to be some large tree roots.

Later in God of War III, when Kratos is eaten by Cronos, he spills the Titan's intestines, making a hole into his belly. But later, when you pierce his jaw with the Onyx that was previously located at his abdomen, you can see that Cronos' intestines are not present and that his belly is not cut open anymore. Even though this event shows Cronos' regenerative power, this may also be considered as a developer error. Another character who displayed regeneration was Erinys, who, after having her wings cut off by Kratos, she quickly grew a new pair.

Prometheus had the ability, but it was probably given to him by Zeus as a punishment, since every time the eagle came to eat his organs, they regenerated, only to be eaten again in the next day by the bird. Baldur displayed some regeneration, both when being cursed and after being vulnerable again.

candidates.title: Einherjar
candidates.text:
The Einherjar are the Norse equivalent of the Olympus Sentry, both of them being the undead main forces of the Gods.
The names of three Einherjar were mentioned when Odin was giving them his blessings. Two male Einherjar are known by the names Hrothgar and Gorm while a female Einherjar is known by the name Jaana.
The Einherjar for the most part have a resemblance to the "War Boys" from Max Max: Fury Road and Mad Max: The Game.
Both have pale skin with black marking around the eye.
Both are "dead", with the War Boys believing in "half-lives" due to the conditions of The Wasteland set after the aftermath of "The Poxy-eclipse" in the Mad Max Universe, meanwhile the Einherjar are reanimated soldiers who died an honorable death and granted access to Valhalla.
Both are related to the concept of Valhalla, with the War Boys believing that being loyal to Immortan Joe and dying in combat will grant them access to the gates of Valhalla where they will "McFeast" with the gods, meanwhile the Einherjar are the result of being granted access to Valhalla proper per a worthy death.

candidates.title: Gods
candidates.text: Greek Gods: Featured prominently in God of War, God of War II, God of War: Betrayal, God of War: Chains of Olympus, God of War III, God of War: Ghost of Sparta, and God of War: Ascension. A great part of the Pantheon was wiped out by Kratos. Initially led by Cronos ruling over the Titan Gods from Mount Orthys, until being overthrown by his son Zeus who ruled over the Olympian Gods from Mount Olympus. Norse Gods: Featured prominently in God of War (2018) and God of War Ragnarök. Split between the warlike Aesir led by the knowledge-hungry Odin and the nature-loving Vanir led by the witch-like Freya. Egyptian Gods: Mentioned in God of War (2018) and God of War Ragnarök, and featured in God of War: Fallen God. They are half-human, half-animal Gods who, from what Mimir heard, rule with wisdom and humility.God of War Ragnarök, Goal: Stolen Treasures, Ankh (Codex Entry) According to Mimir, they are many and not as simple to qualify as "good" or "evil".God of War (2018), Main Quest: "The Journey" - Goal: The Black Rune They are featured on a tapestry showing Týr's journeys and the Egyptian symbol of the Eye_of_Ra Eye of Ra is on Týr's missing triptych panel.God of War (2018), Main Quest: "The Journey" - Goal: A Path to Jötunheim Only the Gods ThothGod of War: Fallen God and SekhmetGod of War Laufey have appeared so far. Egyptian hieroglyphs are also one of the three languages engraved on the Mask of Creation. Mayan Gods: Alluded to in God of War (2018) and mentioned in God of War Ragnarök.

The is an armor set found in God of War Ragnarök.

The armor pieces can be found during the course of the Guiding Light Favor, which can be started by finding one of the pieces. The gauntlets can be found to the northwest of Týr's Temple, around the back of Sindri's shop. The breastplate can be found inside the helmet from Týr's statue on the Lake of Nine. Finally, the waist guard can be found beneath the Hel Bramble, near the Oarsmen, in the area Atreus ventured through earlier in the game.

When worn, the Breastplate of Guiding Light grants Kratos the Weapon Blessing perk, which has a Moderate Luck chance on any hit to increase the Strength, Runic, and Luck of Kratos' weapon. The gauntlets and waist guard each grant the Fortune's Strike perk, which makes melee attacks have a Luck chance to critically strike, resulting in an explosion.

candidates.title: Minotaur
candidates.text: Kratos would once again come across Minotaurs during his travels through Valhalla, having been materialized by the realm to test him. Gameplay-wise, they act like modified Bergsras. However, whereas Bergsras' fire attacks required them to spit smoke and ignite it with a follow-up attack, Minotaurs are capable of a wide-range fire slam. Also, like all Greek enemies, they had a "siphon" attack, an unblockable charge in their case, that upon hit granted them armor which slowly drained Kratos' rage until broken.

candidates.title: QoL Update
candidates.text:
Hello Bananas!

QoL Changes

Today we have some changes regarding QoL (Quality Of Life) changes. That makes it easier to spot different types of bananas inside the game, search and filter them out as well. (The filter does not save between game sessions)

Oh and we've updated the game to reduce the storage usage! (Unninstalling & installing is recommended!)

Normal Bananas - The Huge Quantity

So, we've been seeing, for a while, that the normal banana quantity is still increasing, really fast.
So, we're gonna give it another purpose within the game to make it useful and clean some inventories.
(BTW! There's a delete button if you think you have too many of any banana, you can delete them from your inventory!)

We're changing the usage of the exchanging system to add the requirement of an X amount of normal bananas per rarity of which it's exchanging to, to simplify here's how it goes:

Exchange System Update:

- 10 x Normal > Common - No Change
- 10 x Common [color=lightgreen]+ 2 Normal[/color] > Uncommon
- 10 x Uncommon [color=lightgreen]+ 4 Normal[/color] > Rare
- 10 x Rare [color=lightgreen]+ 8 Normal[/color] > Epic
- 10 x Epic [color=lightgreen]+ 16 Normal[/color] > Ultra Rare
- 10 x Ultra Rare [color=lightgreen]+ 32 Normal[/color] > Legendary

An update is now available on the public open “beta” branch.

The base-game scenario editor has been re-enabled in the beta. We managed to exterminate several bugs based on reports from the previous beta update, special thanks to the testers that took on the fight!

candidates.title: Marvel's Midnight Suns review
candidates.text: I would have highly recommended this game until the June 2023 updates they made. It was on its way to being an underappreciated classic and a favourite to dip back into, much like XCOM 2 (made by the same team).I clocked up a ridiculous number of hours on the Xbox version and was very happy with it - even with the nonsensical DLC release timeline that almost necessitated stopping playing the game until they were all out (eg, if you were 75% of the way through, the new characters came into your game chronically underlevelled and were virtually useless unless you started again). Very happy that is until they made updates that bugged the whole Abbey questline that runs in between the main missions, removing the reward for completing it (I won't explain what that is - spoilers).Firaxis/2K stopped supporting the game after that final June update - even though it was only ONE MONTH after the release of the last DLC and 6-7 months after the game came out. I've ended up buying this PC version on sale just to be able to finish the game the way I would want (there are no user-made mods to fix this on the console versions).To leave a bug like that in all versions of the game for over a year and make no attempt to fix it just screams of something really wrong at how Firaxis, 2K or both view their customers and it irritated me beyond belief. The initial pricing for the game and DLCs seemed really misguided and I'm sure volumes were far lower than they were expecting with a Marvel tie-in and it was career-ending all-round - but if you treat customers like that, they won't trust you again.

candidates.title: Doki Doki Literature Club Plus! review
candidates.text: If you want the tl;dr version, DDLC plus is a prime example of how more is most certainly NOT the same as better. The addition of a 100% progress meter has totally torn the venom out of this slow burn horror game's stinger, and like telling the same joke over and over, has made the original telling of the joke feel worse in retrospect.If you have a little more time on your hands, I'll go point by point. Let's start with the few things I did like.The side scenes were adequate. Nice little character vignettes that in no way contributed to the horror of the game, but provided a small amount of characterisation for those people enamoured by the characters. I'm not among those people, but I assume they would like it.I found myself quite bemused by just how much small variation the original game had in character dialogue, depending on who you wrote poems for and in what order. When fast forwarding through the game, it defaults to stopping on text you've not seen yet, so while I was hammering through the poetry minigame over and over while trying to get the random images to appear for my scrapbook, I got all sorts of combinations I otherwise wouldn't have seen. So, even though the text itself was a feature of the old game, I only KNOW about it because of the new release.Lastly, I quite liked what I believe was a new addition to the first time start screen, strongly clarifying that all of the characters shown were 18 or older. I was never quite as scared with this game as I was while contemplating they had to specify that, with the clear idea that it might have been because of all the porn people have made about these high schoolers.Right, that's the praise out of the way, let's get into the mud.The content warning system is very poor quality. I heard the dev team took inspiration from Ikenfell, a great game that did content warning systems really well?

candidates.title: Total War: ROME REMASTERED review
candidates.text: 《全面战争：罗马 重置版Total War: ROME REMASTERED》是一款策略战术类游戏。 作为颇具盛名的IP《全面战争》系列的第三部作品《罗马：全面战争》的重置版，相较前作除了画质上有了极大程度的提升之外，保证经典的核心玩法不变的前提下也增加了不少可玩派系和一些其他的内容，重置版的出现无疑让不少全战老粉直呼爷青回。 游戏设定在公元前2世纪的古罗马时期，玩家需要做的就是通过内政、外交和战争等手段不断的扩大己方领土，最终朝着一统天下的罗马帝国的目标前进。 核心玩法上，诸如发展经济、建设城池等采用的是经典的回合制玩法，开疆扩土发动战争则是采用的即时战术玩法，二者相辅相成，不仅提升了游戏性还使游戏更加有趣。 一开始可以选择所属势力，不同势力拥有截然不同的玩法及兵种，发展经济部分大同小异，无非就是拼命提升实力为了战争做准备，重点说说战斗方面，在偌大的战场上，需要玩家率先排兵布阵调配好兵力，排好己方军队阵型以及驻守位置，战斗过程中，除了干掉敌人以外，使其军心溃散也是取胜的方法之一，可谓杀人诛心，才是王者之道。 部队中除了普通士兵，当然也会有统帅，且将领们都会有着一定的特性，随着各自经历的不同，不论是常年征战的武将或是管理内务的文臣，都会觉醒不同的特性使其各自的能力成长的愈加强大，也可谓是养成元素满满。

candidates.title: Total War: ROME REMASTERED review
candidates.text: This is a tough one, because my review would normally be a "meh." On the plus side, the improved graphics are a plus. The tooltips to help you manage your empire by locating people, agents, and armies are 100% a useful feature and make managing an empire so much easier than the original game. You can also get more information about factions as you are negotiating with them.On the other hand, it doesn't really go far enough. Do your armies automatically recruit from surrounding settlements to replace losses, like in Shogun 2? No. We don't want the game to be too realistic, now do we? Did they solve the bug where certain naval units won't group with others because the other unit is more experienced, a different type, or is missing a sailor? Nope. Did they solve the issue where siege towers refuse to unload their units? Can't say yet, but probably not!I also had two major bugs in the tutorial- one where it refused to progress me to the next tip, which meant I couldn't continue the campaign, because features in it are unlocked gradually. God forbid a player actually say midway through "nope, I'm good, I don't need help anymore!" And the second bug was my ship insisting "it couldn't sail there" through a green area of water. I'm not asking it to sail to the New World or on land! Just go the nearby island! So they clearly haven't fixed naval navigation completely, either, though it's better than the base game.All in all, I'll probably continue playing it, but it's really not worth the cost I paid. This should be worth 10 bucks max.

candidates.title: Total War: ROME REMASTERED review
candidates.text: OK. Base RTW is probably my favourite strategy game of all time and I was really looking forward to this remaster. I knew going into it that it was just base RTW with a new coat of paint; no overhauled pathfinding, no new units and still scuffed diplomacy etc. To give credit where credit is due, many of the small problems with the game have been addressed like unit rebalancing, making the minor and emergent factions playable and touching up diplomacy. However this is about where my compliments end.OK. As a guy who like to play multiplayer, about 80& of my games have desynced right out of the gate which from the get go means that like half of the game is unplayable (as a fairly big multiplayer guy). Quick loading has crashed my game the 5 times I have instinctively done it. The new UI has various elements I really like but for each addition I like, there is one I don't like. The recruitment and building buttons are in wierd places and creates needless movement from oneside of the ui to the other. Base Romes UI was far from perfect and this is different, not better and arguably worse in many regards.All of this I could accept up until yesterday where my Carthage campaign, which was going really well, became unplayable after I ended turn on turn 28 and it was stuck on the Julii's turn. Then after after reloading multiple times, it would just get stuck on Egypt. This was a real knife in the back.I really want this game to be good, and it seems as if Feral are listening to the playerbase, but in its current state I cannot recommend this game in its current state. Unlike Rome 2 which even after being patched is still really bland and just meh, RTW:R does have the potential to be really good and am more than willing to change this review down the line, but for now I don't think I will be playing this mess.

candidates.title: Total War: ROME REMASTERED review
candidates.text: I had a lot of fun with this remastered version of Rome: Total War. But I have to wonder if it really gave much added value over the original game. Yes you can play all the factions here - but with simple modding you could do that in the base game. Yes it has better gameplay - but the AI is still seemingly suffering in executing amphibious attacks or finding a path around in the steppes. This isn't to say there isn't some nice stuff here though. The camera improvements are certainly nice and being able to see information on an icon above ones troops when in battle is certainly convenient. I also like some of the little tweeks that enable changes to the gameplay - that you can turn on and off as you please; so horray, I can turn off those stupid Merchants, but leave the rest in!But is it worth the price? I can't say it really felt like it was worth the value in comparison to having already owned the previous game. Those with newer computers might not be able to run the original game though, so that might be a consideration for picking up this game; that and never having actually 'played' the original.I will note that in playing this game that I didn't experience any real issues. I had a rare crash here and there - but after 200+ hours of game time, I can't actually say it was worse then the original, which also tended to crash here and there.

candidates.title: Total War: ROME REMASTERED review
candidates.text: This is a fun game for gamers who enjoy both strategic and tactical aspects of strategy games. The game is not perfect by any means, but it is one I can always come back to after 6 months off and enjoy a few months of gameplay before it gets old again.The strategic aspect is not that challenging. If you play as the Seleucid, Egypt or any of the three Roman factions you should be able to win the game once you understand the basics. The Seleucid are my favorite group to play with. They are basically unbeatable when defending a city and they also get access to War Elephants.I do wish that population was not such a burden. Basically, you have to massacre civilians throughout the game. This includes when you take a city or even letting revolts take place and razing the city afterwards. There is also basically no naval warfare after a certain point in the game. Finally, if you play as any of the three Roman factions, you basically plan your entire strategy around getting ready to be stabbed in the back. If you play as the Bruti for example, try to gain cities within the Julli and Scippi territories. I also like to keep a huge stack on the Italian peninsula for when that takes place.Overall, recommend for any player. Great for people who like to stay at a high level and also great for people who like to manage every detail.

candidates.title: Total War: ROME REMASTERED review

After about 60 hours of play, I've finished the Julii long campaign and a short campaign with my beloved Dacia, I can say a few things about this game, so here it is:At this stage, I would not recomend buying this as it doesn't offer too much over the original. Ups:-better graphic (duh!)- merchants from Medieval II- 5% better diplomacy, and I'm being generous- moving retinue membersand that's about it. Downs:- the UI is soooo convoluted and counter-intuitive, I have to check in 5 places, open 10 submenus to find out 1 damn thing. It's horrible. When I had more than 20 provinces, to go through them was a nightmare. The whole overlay is bad, with little options, that stupid menu with details about characters that raises, has a tiny X mark that you have to aim for. Also, the percentages are bogus, 50% of the time I lose takeovers with 95% chance. - same stupid way the family members get traits and retinue (drunken uncle and crap like that keeps showing up)- still 5 buildings you can build in barbarian villages. candidates.title: Total War: ROME REMASTERED review
candidates.text: I have a cumulative 3500+ hours invested in Total War games since 2012. I speak with some authority when it comes to the mechanics in these games. This review however isn't directed at new players, but experienced, returning total war fans. I have played the Remaster for only 10 hours, and I have already encountered game breaking problems that make it impossible for me to take the game seriously, whether in Campaign or in Multiplayer.The primary issue is with how they coded the physics for battles on top of the existing engine. They have thoroughly and irreparably messed up the fluidity of combat. Particularly, phalanges have been affected the most by this, becoming totally impotent, nearly to the level of Rome 2, a fact which I'm sure everyone who played that game is intimately aware of. The problems are fundamental, they lie in how the path-finding, unit cohesion, and unit reforming work. The result is that this is no longer Rome: Total War, but some sort of bastard child resembling Rome 1, but playing like Rome 2.Case in point, the Multiplayer community has already moved back to the original. On launch day there were 10 lobbies concurrently. Only a few days later there were no more than 2, which is the same number as on Rome, a game released in 2004.What enrages me the most isn't how totally they have ruined one of my favorite games of all time, but that they've done so while taking away the right to buy the original. We will no longer have new Rome: Total War players. We will only have new Total War: Rome Remastered players, who in all likelihood will never even realize they're buying the superior, original games as part of a bundle for $30 alongside it, or if they do, they will think them inferior, graphically or otherwise. The better game will die in obscurity. Rome managed to survive for nearly 20 years having been left alone by Creative Assembly.

candidates.title: Total War: ROME REMASTERED review
candidates.text: Total War: Rome Remastered is the remaster of the classic 2004 game Rome: Total War. Take over Europe, Northern Africa, and the middle east as one of three available Roman factions, or take up arms against the Roman as almost every faction in the game!PROS:~For $30 ($15 if you bought it while owning Rome: Total War) This is definitely a bargain. You get the original game with all its DLC, AND the remaster with all its DLC. Its essentially 6 games in one~The remaster isnt identical to the original. There are a lot of additions and quality of life changes, such as the addition of merchants, limit on squalor penalty, and the ability to remove the leaves from trees. Of course, you can disable ALL of them for the original but with better graphics~There is proper workshop support, which is much easier than trying to install mods yourself, and the mods available as of this review completely change the game already~I hear people complain about the vibrancy of the graphics, but you can change the graphics to more realistic graphics, so thats a problem solved~You can play just about every faction from barbarian invasion and the original rome total war (apart from the rebels and the S.P.Q.R) which adds a lot more fun opportunities and gameplays~There are a FEW new soundtracks, which is nice and adds a bit of difference in the music.CONS:~I've noticed that, for Barbarian invasion especially, the game crashes quite often if you play as a faction that wasn't originally available (at least when I played the Celts)~There are a lot of assets that are completely unchanged, mainly the pictures with events. I would love at least a re-rendering of those in the style of the game itself~Some of the new available factions have not really been made to be played.
